On the problem I went past the seat's measureText heuristic and parsed the cmap out of the three vendored woff2 files directly (brotli-decompress, walk the table directory, read format-4/12 subtables): Geist-Regular, Geist-SemiBold and GeistMono-Regular each map 726/726/887 codepoints and NONE of them carries U+2302, U+270E or U+2611; all three carry U+2197. So three of the four marks in shell()'s `<nav class="rail">` (lately.html:710) are painted by an OS fallback, not by a face the studio chose. The inherited stack is `"Geist", system-ui, sans-serif` (lately.html:117), and .rail i (lately.html:157) only sets font-size 13px, so nothing intercepts the fallback. The audit really is blind to it: audit.mjs:256 reads `cs.fontFamily.split(",")[0]`, i.e. the authored family, never the painted one. I also swept every rendered codepoint >= U+2000 across all seven states and the seat's scope claim holds exactly - U+2019, U+2014 and U+00B7 are all in Geist's cmap, so these four marks are the only text on the surface outside the two locked faces. And it is visible, not theoretical: a 4x capture of the rail shows the fallback pencil rendering as a SOLID FILLED shape against three outline marks, at a stroke weight and drawing convention matching nothing in ICON. SEVERITY is understated, not overstated: the seat filed refinement ("nothing is wrong"), but a filled glyph sitting in a four-item stack of outlines, drawn by a face outside the two the lock permits and changing per OS, is visibly wrong - this is a defect. One sub-claim does not reproduce here: I sampled the rail region at 4x for any pixel with saturation > 0.12 and found zero, so on this Windows build U+2611 resolves to a monochrome Segoe UI Symbol, not an emoji face. The seat hedged that as conditional, so it is not an error, but it is not evidence either. WHAT FAILS IS THE FIX. "Inline SVG paths at 13px ... on the same 12x12 grid as ICON" is self-contradictory and mis-sized. ICON's marks are authored `<svg width="12" height="12" viewBox="0 0 12 12">`, so they render at 12px and the "13px" is either ignored or, if forced, scales a 12-unit grid by 1.0833 and lands ICON's 1.5-1.6 strokes at 1.625 device px off the pixel grid at 1x - blurring hairlines on a surface whose entire icon system is deliberately integer-snapped. Worse, 12x12 is the wrong grid for this tile regardless of the scaling: .glyph chips are 20x20 carrying 12px marks (ratio 0.60), while .rail i is 26x26 (measured 26x26 at 1440). A 12px mark in a 26px tile is ratio 0.46 - the four rail marks would land visibly smaller and lighter than every other chip on the surface, and lighter than the fallback glyphs they replace, which optically fill ~14-15px today. The fix direction is right; its two numbers are both wrong.
confirmed.sharpenedFix: Keep the direction - replace the four characters in shell()'s .rail markup with inline SVG in currentColor, aria-hidden, authored in ICON's stroke language - but fix the geometry. Draw on a 16x16 grid rendered at exactly 16px (`<svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16">`), integer 1:1, which holds the 0.60 mark-to-tile ratio the 20px .glyph chips already establish (16/26 = 0.62). Hold stroke-width at 1.5 with stroke-linecap/linejoin round, identical to ICON.still/past/nobody/waiting, so the rail reads as the same pen rather than a scaled-up copy. Use `stroke="currentColor"` only - never ICON's hard-coded status hexes, which are reserved for the four status meanings and would import amber/red/indigo/emerald into inert furniture. currentColor is required, not optional, because .rail i.on inverts to color:var(--paper) on background:var(--ink). Then drop `font-size: 13px` from the .rail i rule: it no longer sets any type, and leaving a dead type declaration on a textless element is the kind of residue this lock exists to prevent. Redraw all four (including the arrow, which Geist does carry) so the set is one system, not three vectors beside one survivor.
confirmed.breaks: Nothing in the behaviour gate: interaction-check.mjs contains no assertion touching .rail, and the nav is aria-hidden="true" so no accessible name, tab stop or focus order changes. The audit is where to re-measure. audit.mjs gates its family, weight, type-ramp and leading checks on `hasText && visible` (audit.mjs:253), so all four .rail i elements currently supply samples and would drop out entirely once the text is gone. Two consequences to re-run for: (1) the leading role-key map is keyed family|size|role (audit.mjs:287) - .rail i is presently a Geist|13|body occupant, and removing it changes which element is recorded as first-seen for that key, so re-run the audit and confirm no new leading collision surfaces elsewhere at 13px; (2) the AA contrast sample for ink-2 on --wash inside the rail chip disappears, because SVG strokes are not contrast-checked. That makes the gate easier, not harder, which is exactly the trap: verify by eye at 1x that 1.5px strokes in var(--ink-2) do not read lighter than the filled fallback glyphs they replace, and that the inverted .rail i.on mark in var(--paper) on var(--ink) still holds its weight. Also re-shoot light-full at 768x1024 and 1280x900 - the rail is display:none only below 560px, so it is in-frame at both - and re-run the dark variant, since currentColor inverts there and a stroke tuned on paper can go thin on ground. Palette is untouched: currentColor introduces no nineteenth hue.

confirmed.element: The tab strip - "Today's Signal", "Full briefing", "Lately"
confirmed.problem: Two sibling destinations, both proper names of surfaces in this product, are capitalised by two different rules on the same line. The signed-in naming contract names it the Full Briefing.
confirmed.consequence: One of the three destinations is demoted from a name to a description, in every state and both grounds, on the most-read line of the page. It is the kind of inconsistency the benchmark products never ship, and once seen it is visible every time.
confirmed.fix: Render the tab "Full Briefing", matching Today's Signal and the naming contract.
confirmed.assertion: In every state and both grounds the tab strip's three labels are exactly "Today's Signal", "Full Briefing" and "Lately".
confirmed.verdict: Verified in source and frames. lately.html line 721 renders `Full briefing` next to `Today’s Signal` on line 720; the light-full frames at 1440 and 390 show 'Today's Signal Full briefing Lately' exactly as claimed. This is not taste: the repo's own URL and naming contract (docs/SUITE_URL_AND_NAMING_CONTRACT.md, lines 18 and 57-58) states the briefing surfaces are named 'Today's Signal' (inside Home) and 'Full Briefing' (/app/home/briefing), and this brief's own non-negotiable architecture clause writes 'a tab strip beside Today's Signal and the Full Briefing'. The artifact also capitalises every other product name it prints (Tasks, Timeline, Notes in the coverage row), so sentence case here is not a house rule the tab is following - it is the one label out of step. The string lives in the shared shell() template, so it is wrong in all seven states and both grounds, on the page's second line. Neither gate touches it: audit.mjs has no copy assertion and interaction-check.mjs never reads the tab text, so this is exactly the class of defect automation cannot see. Severity is corrected upward from the seat's 'refinement' to 'defect': by the panel's own definitions refinement means nothing is wrong, and here the product misnames one of its own surfaces against a written contract - visibly wrong, but the reader still reaches the right place, so it stops short of misleading. The proposed fix is the right one and needs no sharpening: one character, matching the contract and the sibling tab.
confirmed.breaks: Nothing structural. The change is one glyph ('b' to 'B') in the shell() template, adding roughly 1px to the tab's advance width; the 390x844 frame shows the strip ending well short of the fold, so there is no wrap or overflow risk at the narrow end, and 768/1280/1440 have more room still. Re-measure after it lands: run audit.mjs (type ramp, leading and hit-target checks touch the tab strip's box) and re-shoot the seven light states plus the dark ground, since the string is shared by all of them - a diff on any one state that does not move by the same sub-pixel amount would mean the label is duplicated somewhere the grep missed. Worth chasing in the same cycle for consistency, though outside the graded artifact: plan.html line 387 prints 'Full briefing' in its own prose.

refuted.problem: The reading line is part of the shell, so "Twelve weeks" prints unconditionally. I drove all seven states: first-run draws one column and says Twelve weeks; empty draws no chart at all and says Twelve weeks; error draws nothing, says "Tasks did not answer", and still says Read at 09:14 and Twelve weeks at the top — the same instant the card below calls the last good reading.
refuted.why: The mechanism is real - shell() at lately.html:724-728 prints 'Read at ${D.readingLong}' and a hard-coded 'Twelve weeks' for all seven states - but the finding is factually wrong about two of the three states it indicts, and the severity is overstated by two classes. EMPTY: the finding says 'the surface states the scope of a reading that never happened.' It did happen. SOURCES.empty is { tasks: 'answered, nothing recorded' }, and the coverage strip in the frame reads TASKS ANSWERED, NOTHING RECORDED. Tasks was asked, at 09:14, over twelve weeks, and returned no records. 'Read at 09:14' and 'Twelve weeks' are both literally true there; that is the honest-degradation contract working, not breaching. ERROR: the finding claims the header 'still says Read at 09:14 ... the same instant the card below calls the last good reading' as if that were a contradiction. Both strings are the same accessor, D.readingLong, and the fixture holds exactly one reading instant. The header is not asserting a fresh successful read at a time the card denies - it is the last good reading printed once at the top, which is precisely what the behaviour gate's 'unanchored time' block (interaction-check.mjs:336-350) exists to require in the error state. Ambiguous wording, not an untruth. FIRST-RUN: this is the one live sub-claim, and it is weaker than stated. 'Twelve weeks' reads as the window of the view - the lookback the Lately tab performs - not as a claim that twelve weeks of records exist; a 'Last 12 weeks' range label over a sparse series is standard at every named benchmark. And the state does not draw eleven zeros: the plot contains a baseline and one centred column, no gridlines, no eleven empty slots, so nothing fabricates the zero the contract forbids. The card then names the account's age twice in the reader's own words - '12 jobs finished since you started' and 'Four weeks of records make a comparison worth printing. Yours arrive on 10 August.' The 'you did nothing for nearly three months' inference has to survive both of those, on the same card, to land. The declared class is 'misleading = the product asserts something untrue'; nothing here is untrue. At most this is a refinement in the header's precision on one of seven states. THE FIX IS ALSO WRONG AGAINST THE SOURCE. 'Derive the scope label from the weeks actually drawn, in the same one-accessor discipline as every other fact' cannot be done from D: D.weeks is F.weeks, always twelve entries in every state including first-run and empty - first-run is a presentational branch that renders D.weeks[11] alone (lately.html:781). There is no drawnWeeks to read. And the error half of the fix makes the surface worse: 'Asked at 09:14' beside 'Last good reading - 09:14' would assert that the failed request and the last success happened at the same instant, manufacturing the contradiction the finding wrongly claims already exists. Correct problem, wrong fix, wrong class - refuted, with the salvageable part sharpened below.

refuted.problem: The caption is laid over the marks. Measured at 1440: "and it stays empty until the recorder has run for three periods." intersects 6 of the 12 ghost columns and the head "This is the chart we would draw" intersects 1, because .ghost-say is position: absolute; inset: 0 centred over a .ghost-plot drawn at opacity 0.5. The columns themselves are var(--wash) with a 1px dashed top and no baseline, so at 50% opacity behind text they do not read as a chart at all — they read as pale blocks behind a sentence.
refuted.why: The arithmetic checks out and the perceptual claim it rests on does not. Driven at 1440 the small line spans x565.1-930.9 y1668.8-1685.8 and intersects exactly 6 of the 12 columns; the head spans x602.4-893.6 y1604.8-1630.8 and intersects exactly 1. So the counts are right. But the conclusion drawn from them is wrong against the pixels. Every column top sits between y1619.4 and y1657.8, all of them ABOVE the caption's top edge of y1668.8 - so the caption crosses no top edge, no dash, no silhouette; it lies entirely inside the flat fill body of the bars it spans. The head at y1604.8-1630.8 clears the skyline but for the single tallest column at y1619.4. That is not a collision, it is a composition: the head sits above the skyline, the caption sits in the dead fill below it. Rendered at 1440 and at 390 the twelve columns read unmistakably as a bar chart - shared baseline, uniform width and gap, rounded tops, a rising silhouette - with a caption set inside it, the ordinary watermark idiom. No text is obscured and no mark is destroyed. 'They do not read as a chart at all' and 'reads as a rendering error' are simply not what the frames show. Severity 'defect' - visibly wrong but passable - is therefore overstated; nothing is visibly wrong. Refinement at most. The proposed fix is also wrong twice over, and the second way is serious. First the numbers: the fix assumes 'full opacity' recovers a real chart, but --wash is rgba(17,17,17,0.03), so dropping opacity 0.5 takes the fill from ~1.5% to 3% ink (#fbfbfb to #f8f8f8) and the dashed top from 5% to 10%. It stays a whisper. To buy the reading the fix promises you would also have to darken the wash, which is a new stated-alpha tint and a fresh audit run. Second, and this is why it must not land: the twelve heights are invented - 38,52,44,61,47,58,50,66,54,62,57,70, a rising trend. Today the 0.5 opacity and the caption lying across the fill are exactly what mark that silhouette as a placeholder rather than a reading. Full opacity plus a real baseline rule plus 'its own faint value axis' - a scale for data that does not exist - converts a deliberately spectral placeholder into something that presents as a plotted upward trend over twelve periods, inside the one movement whose whole job is to refuse to draw that trend. That is the honest-degradation contract inverted: not a fabricated zero, a fabricated rise. The protected object is 'the trend the product cannot produce is drawn as the chart it would be' - would be, conditional, and the transparency is carrying that conditional. Removing it to gain legibility trades the idea for the rendering.

refuted.problem: The entrance animates opacity from 0 with staggered delays (rise up to 260ms delay, .dot::before up to 760ms + 55ms per mark) while every control is focusable from the first frame. Measured at ?motion=play: 1203ms elapse before no focusable element is at effective opacity below 0.1 — 12 invisible focusables at ready, still 3 at 900ms. Four Tab presses immediately after __LATELY_READY land on the "3 haven't moved in a fortnight" KPI link at effective opacity 0.000; its 2px focus outline inherits that opacity, so nothing at all is painted. The behaviour gate's "nothing invisible can take focus" rule runs on the settled surface (default under webdriver), so this condition has never been evaluated by it — the same blind-gate class as the coarse-pointer and sub-720px misses in the defect library.
refuted.why: The central measurement is wrong, and it is wrong in a way that inverts the consequence. Driven at ?motion=play, 1440x960, sampling every focusable (a[href], button, [tabindex]) with ancestor opacity multiplied in: every focusable ELEMENT is at effective opacity >= 0.1 at 192ms after __LATELY_READY, >= 0.5 at 242ms, >= 0.9 at 360ms. Not 1203ms, and nothing is below 0.1 at 900ms - the seat's 'still 3 at 900ms' is false. I reproduced the seat's 1203ms figure exactly (1193ms) only by multiplying in getComputedStyle(el, '::before').opacity, which proves what was actually measured: .dot::before, the decorative disc. The disc is not the focusable and does not carry the ring. lately.html:301 says so in the source comment - 'The disc is a pseudo, not the button' - a deliberate earlier fix so the control's geometry survives its own entrance. The .dot button is fully laid out from the first frame; .dot:focus-visible paints 2px solid #4f46e5 at offset 3px on it (verified computed on a focused dot at t=59ms), and focusing a dot also fires show(el), raising the tooltip with the job title - the tip is outside #root, carries no rise, and is at full opacity. So on the dots, which are 9 of the 12 controls the seat counted, focus is not only visible, it is annotated. The claim that there is 'no way to tell whether focus has entered the page' is contradicted by the surface. What is left is the KPI links, and their exposure is unreachable in practice. The tab sequence opens with three static header tab links (lately.html:720-722) at opacity 1, which absorb Tabs 1-3, so a person's first Tab always lands on painted ink. Tab 4 reaches a.kpi.rise, whose worst delay is 65ms with a 500ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1) ease-out. Driving four presses at 40ms apart - faster than any keyboard's autorepeat first interval, which is 250-500ms - lands at opacity 0.805; at 80ms, 0.993; at 150ms, 1.000. The seat's 'opacity 0.000' reproduces only by firing four presses inside 8ms, which is a Playwright artefact, not a human input path. The residue is real but tiny: for roughly the first 190ms the ring on a KPI card is dimmed rather than absent. That is a refinement, not a defect, and an overstated class is on its own grounds for refusal here. The seat is right that interaction-check.mjs:107-117 evaluates 'nothing invisible can take focus' on the settled surface using the element's own computed opacity, so this transient has never been gated - but a blind gate is only worth a finding if something is behind it, and what is behind it is 190ms of a fading ring on cards that Tab cannot reach that fast.

refuted.problem: Six places where the source no longer describes the file. (1) `.bar.live { background: var(--accent) }` — the live class is only applied when the last week is not partial, and the fixture's last week is always partial; `document.querySelectorAll('.bar.live').length` is 0 in every one of the seven states. (2) `@media (max-width: 900px) { .sk-row { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr) } }` — no `.sk-row` element exists anywhere; it was left behind when the skeleton was rewritten to reuse the real components. (3) `.meter i.zero { background: var(--mark-ctx) }` — the class is applied when n is 0, but the same branch sets `--f: 0`, so the element is `scaleX(0)` and the colour can never paint. (4) The CSS comment 'Three gridlines, not a grid' and the JS comment 'Three gridlines with their values' both sit above `[0.5, 1].map(...)`, which draws two; the behaviour gate matches the code (`grid.n >= 2`) rather than the comment. (5) `@media (max-width: 560px) { .t-hero { font-size: 64px } }` restates the base value and changes nothing. (6) The first-run hero numeral has no `id="count"`, so the count-up entrance the comment calls 'the moment' runs in six states of seven.
refuted.why: Driven in chromium across all seven states at 1440 and read against the source. Five of the six sub-claims are factually right. (1) document.querySelectorAll('.bar.live').length is 0 in all seven states, and the rule is unreachable by design rather than by fixture: the last column is the current week, and the protected partial-bucket contract makes the current week always partial, so the live branch of the ternary at line 559 can never be taken. (2) No .sk-row exists in any state; line 440 is dead. The finding caught the rule and missed that the block comment at line 365 also describes an '.sk-in block' that does not exist either (0 matches in every state) - the same class of staleness, one line above the rewrite it survived. (3) .meter i.zero really is emitted (D.waiting is 0, so it appears in full, partial, first-run and loading) but the same branch sets --f:0; computed transform is matrix(0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0) at width 0, so var(--mark-ctx) cannot paint. (5) The 560px .t-hero override restates the base: computed font-size is 64px at 390, 561 and 1440. (6) The first-run hero numeral has no id='count'. The finding is refuted on its fix and on one of its stated facts. FACT: the count-up does not 'run in six states of seven'. It runs in three - full, partial, quiet. Loading is excluded deliberately at line 867, and empty and error render no hero numeral at all, so the real gap is one state out of the four that have one. FIX, item 6, is the decisive error: adding id='count' to the first-run hero makes it count 12 up from Math.max(0, 12 - 12) = 0, so the one state whose entire message is 'you have started' would open on a literal 0, and for 700ms the numeral would disagree with the '12 so far' bar label sitting directly beneath it inside the same card - exactly the self-contradiction the file's own header comment at line 459 exists to prevent. The from = target - 12 heuristic is tuned for the 31 of the full-state hero and degenerates on a low-teens figure. FIX, item 4, is half-aimed: the CSS comment 'Three gridlines, not a grid' is defensible as written, because the plot does rule three horizontal lines - two .gridline plus .baseline - and only the value-bearing ones carry the class; it is the JS comment 'Three gridlines with their values' that is wrong, since gridline b count is 2. Offering 'render a third at 0.25' as an equal alternative puts a design change on the table to satisfy a comment, and adding scaffolding to a chart whose own comment says more than three lines compete with the marks would make the work worse. FIX, items 1 and 3, delete only the CSS and leave the dead 'live ? bar live : bar' branch and the purposeless n === 0 ? 'zero' : '' emission in the JS - which reproduces the exact 'reads as a live decision' problem the finding is about, one layer down. Severity 'refinement' is correctly classed: nothing on screen is wrong in any state.

refuted.problem: The micro-label voice (11px Geist Mono, weight 400, `letter-spacing: 0.09em`, uppercase) has no upper bound on string length, and the longest string on the surface is set in it. The `.coverage` block carries 246–267 characters of `data-type="label"` depending on state, of which the lab clause alone is 134: "LAB WEEKLY COUNTS AND AGES ARE LAB-AUTHORED; HARBOUR HOUSE WEDDINGS, ORLA, THE READING DATE AND THE 9 ARE BOUND TO THE SHIPPING FIXTURE". At 390 it renders as a four-line, 133px-tall paragraph of tracked uppercase mono. Every other label on the surface is a stamp of 12–36 characters, which is what the voice is for; this one is a sentence with a semicolon and three clauses. Tracked uppercase mono destroys word shape, and word shape is what makes a sentence scannable — the two are directly opposed.
refuted.why: The typographic observation is half right and everything built on top of it is wrong. Measured in the browser at file://.../lately.html?v=light&state=<state>: .coverage is 11px Geist Mono, letter-spacing 0.99px (0.09em), line-height 14.85px, uppercase, colour #71717a - the voice is as described, and the lab clause is 135 characters, wrapping to four lines (59px) at 390 and two lines (30px) at 768. That much stands. The rest does not. (1) The character counts are inflated: the seat claims the block carries 246-267 characters across states; measured it is 214-235 (full 226, partial 232, quiet 226, first-run 226, empty 235, loading 214, error 223). (2) The 133px is the whole strip - four one-line source stamps plus the clause - not 'a 133px-tall paragraph'; the paragraph is 59px. The complaint is stated at 2.25x its actual size. (3) The load-bearing claim is misattributed. The seat calls this 'the surface's own honesty statement, and the thing a sceptical owner would look for'. It is not. The product's honesty disclosure is the protected 'What this can't tell you' movement, the honest-degradation contract, and the four source stamps that precede this clause (TASKS ANSWERED, TIMELINE ANSWERED, NOTES ANSWERED FOR YOU, READ 09:14...) - each 14-33 characters, one line each, which the seat itself concedes are correctly set. The clause it objects to reads 'weekly counts and ages are lab-authored; Harbour House weddings, Orla, the reading date and the 9 are bound to the shipping fixture' - that is lab-fixture provenance addressed to this panel, naming which numbers were authored for the design lab. A venue owner never reads it, because in the shipped product no numbers are lab-authored. With the false consequence removed, what is left is lab furniture wrapping at two of ten frames - the audit gate already carves out exactly this category (.tl-caption and clip-path furniture are excluded from the letterfit ladder); this string simply is not tagged as furniture. That is a refinement, not a defect. (4) The proposed fix is measurably worse and I drove it to confirm. .t-small sets size, leading and tracking but NOT font-family, and the span sits inside .coverage.t-label which sets font-family: 'Geist Mono'; font-family inherits. Applying the fix verbatim yields computed 13px "Geist Mono" - still mono, now 2px LARGER than the four product source stamps beside it, so the least important string on the surface becomes the largest text in the strip and the hierarchy inverts. And the strip grows at every breakpoint, not shrinks: 133 -> 154px at 390, 84 -> 95px at 768, 51 -> 76px at 1440, because flex:1 1 100% forces its own row where the clause currently sits inline as a single 15px line on desktop, and max-width:68ch at 13px mono is 530px, which wraps it to two 20.15px lines. Seven of the ten named frames are 768 or wider; the fix damages all of them to address a 390-only wrap. 'dim' is also a no-op - .coverage is already color: var(--ink-3) and .dim is var(--ink-3). A correct problem with a wrong fix is refuted, and here the problem is also overstated and mis-consequenced.

refuted.problem: Eleven of the twelve columns give the reader no number by any means. Driven at 1440: no .colw is focusable, none carries data-tip or title, and the only visible value on the plot is the live column's "12 so far". Magnitude is available only by eye against two gridlines at 6 and 12. In the same card, and in the ages strip one section below, every single dot names its fact on hover, on touch and on focus — so one surface teaches the reader that marks answer when you point at them, and its largest chart does not.
refuted.why: Two of the finding's load-bearing factual claims are wrong when driven, and the consequence it derives from them is wrong as well. (1) "Eleven of the twelve columns give the reader no number by any means" is false: chart() emits a full sr paragraph reading "27 Apr, 5; 4 May, 3; 11 May, 6; 18 May, 4; 25 May, 7; 1 Jun, 5; 8 Jun, 8; 15 Jun, 6; 22 Jun, 6; 29 Jun, 8; 6 Jul, 5; 13 Jul, 12 so far" — every one of the twelve is named, and that is the keyboard/AT reading of the plot. (2) "the only visible value on the plot is the live column's '12 so far'" is false: measured at 1440 the plot also paints gridline values 6 and 12 and the record tag "Best week · 8", so three magnitudes are labelled, not one. (3) The consequence — that a reader "cannot read what a good week looks like for them" — is the one thing the plot answers most explicitly. The record line IS that answer, drawn at its own height and labelled 8, and five of the eleven complete columns land exactly on a labelled reference (three at the 6 gridline, two on the record line at 8). The residual six sit between 0 and 6 on a 168px plot where one job is 14px; that is estimation, but it is not "no number". The severity is also overstated. Nothing on this chart is visibly wrong — it has a baseline, valued gridlines, a labelled record, a dated axis, a labelled live column and a complete spoken enumeration. What is proposed is an addition, so the class is refinement, not defect, and an overstated class is on its own grounds for refusal here. The residue that IS true — a fine-pointer user gets a per-week readout from the dots and not from the columns — is worth a refinement, but not by the fix as written. The fix's own numbers are right (8 Jun = 8 in the fixture) and it does not touch a constraint; it is the mechanism that fails. It claims "the existing show/place/hide model with no new code path", and that is exactly what will not work: place() anchors the tip to el.getBoundingClientRect(), and .colw measures 168px tall at every width (it is the full plot band). A tip bound to .colw is placed above or below the whole plot, i.e. up to 168px away from the bar it names — for the 3-job week of 4 May, a 42px bar, the tip floats four bar-heights above its own mark. Correct placement requires anchoring to .bar while hovering .colw, which is a new code path, not the existing one.

refuted.problem: The product's one named threshold is fourteen days, and it is what three of the five status cards are counted on. The axis is ruled in fives, so the threshold line stands one day left of a 15d tick and its label prints directly above it, 40px apart at 1440 and closer at 768.
refuted.why: The observation is half-right and the consequence is wrong. Right: lately.html:622 builds marks = [0, 15, 30, 45] and the fortnight line sits at 14/axisMax; driven at 1440 the dashed line lands at x=321.7 in a 1034px strip while the "15d" label box starts at 347.2 (centre 358.7), and at 768 the edge gap narrows to 15px. Wrong: there is no 15d tick. .strip-axis is a single hairline with no marks on it; .strip-scale is a row of four floating labels. The fortnight rule is the ONLY vertical mark in the strip, so it cannot be misread as one of a series of ticks that does not exist. Wrong again on the reader's task: nobody rules the threshold off this axis. Membership is encoded on the mark itself (.dot.old paints the disc in accent for age >= fortnight, lately.html:619), stated per-dot on hover and focus ("19 days open") and in the aria-label, summarised in the KPI card, restated in the sr paragraph, and interaction-check.mjs:330 already proves the accent marks past the line equal the number the card claims. The seat's own scenario fails on the frames too: the label reads "A fortnight", a word, never a numeral, so there is no 14-versus-15 arithmetic on screen to get wrong, and a 14-day job would sit ON the line with an accent fill, not on the wrong side of it. The frame's ages are 2,3,5,6,9,11,19,23,41 - the nearest mark to the line is 3 days clear. The declared class is right: refinement, nothing is wrong. What is actually wrong in this strip is something the seat walked past: .strip-scale is display:flex; justify-content:space-between, so the labels are distributed by box width, not placed at their values. Even now the "15d" centre prints 14px (0.6 of a day) right of the true 15-day position, and the moment axisMax leaves 45 - it is derived, Math.max(45, ceil((oldest+4)/5)*5) at line 489 - a 60-day job gives axisMax 65 and the four labels still print at 0/33/67/100% while their values sit at 0/23/46/69%. That is a scale label lying about its own position, which is misleading, not refinement.

refuted.problem: The one animated numeral on the page counts from `target - 12` — 19 on this fixture — to 31 over 700ms. Nineteen is not a fact. The number it should count from is on screen two centimetres away: the delta pill says "+5 on the four before", so the four before is 26, and 26 is a real figure the reader can be shown earning its way to 31.
refuted.why: The code reading is right and the class is right, but the fix does not deliver the effect it is sold on and would break a green gate. Verified in the source: lately.html:871 is `const from = Math.max(0, target - 12)`, target is D.lastFour = 6+8+5+12 = 31, D.priorFour = 7+5+8+6 = 26, D.delta = +5, so the count does run 19 to 31. What the seat has not tested is whether a start value is legible as a fact. Driving the master at motion=play and sampling #count every frame, the numeral is already past 23 by the time a sampler attached one tick after load, and it transitions through nine values before landing. Nobody reads the first frame of a 96px numeral as an assertion, so swapping 19 for 26 does not perform the argument — it swaps one unread start frame for another. Worse, it swaps an inert number for a plausible wrong total: 26 is a real answer to a different question, printed in the slot whose meaning is 'jobs finished in the last four weeks'. interaction-check.mjs:538 states the contract in its own comment — 'the count-up must never show a number the reader could mistake for the answer' — and 26 is precisely more mistakable than 19, not less. Three further faults in the fix as written. First, 700ms is calibrated to a twelve-integer distance; held at 700ms over five integers the count lands at 384ms and then sits dead on 31 for the remaining 316ms, and renders six distinct values instead of thirteen — a stutter, not a count. Second, 'when the delta is negative the count runs down' directly violates interaction-check.mjs:519, `ok("the figure counts up from below and never overshoots", early.hero <= late.hero)`, which is green today; it would put a numeral larger than the true total in the hero slot, which is the misleading class this master already guards. Third, tying the start to the data makes the page's only choreography data-dependent: when last four equals prior four the count-up becomes a no-op and the moment vanishes, where `target - 12` always animates. The opacity-0 delta pill is also specified without the settled override the master already establishes for exactly this at lately.html:428 (`[data-motion="settled"] .record { clip-path: none; opacity: 1; }`); as written the '+5 on the four before' would be invisible in all ten frames in shots/, in the audit gate's composited-contrast capture, and to every reduced-motion reader, because PLAY is false under webdriver (lately.html:841). Severity refinement is correctly declared and not overstated — nothing on the surface is wrong today — so this gates nothing either way.

rounds.headline: Clean on severity: both misleading claims were refuted and reclassified, so round 2 confirms nothing blocking and nothing misleading. It is not clean on the other two clauses. Self-inflicted cost is 36% — five of fourteen confirmed findings land on work built during round 1's remediation — and the surface was not frozen: this round restructured the scroll model, rebuilt the loading state and took the link role off the KPI row. The round's most valuable output was again in the instrument rather than the surface: two round-1 assertions were vacuous, one grepping a stylesheet for a selector it never rendered and three comparing the loading DOM against itself.

confirmed.element: a.kpi:hover / a.kpi:active (lately.html:323, :325) against .rise (:485)
confirmed.problem: `.rise` sets `animation: rise 0.5s var(--ease) both`, and rise's `to` frame is `{ opacity: 1; transform: none }`. A filled animation sits in the animation origin, which outranks any plain author declaration, so `transform` on every .rise element is pinned to `none` forever. The KPI cards carry `.rise`, so `a.kpi:hover { transform: translateY(-2px) }` has never painted. Driven with real pointer travel and a held mouse-down in all three motion modes — settled (automation default), ?motion=play, and prefers-reduced-motion — the computed transform on a.kpi read matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0) at rest, on hover and on press, identically. The press is dead twice over: `a.kpi:active { transform: translateY(0) }` is the rest value anyway, so even released it would change nothing. The whole hover channel that survives is a 1px border stepping rgba(17,17,17,0.055) → 0.10 (#f2f2f2 → #e8e8e8 on white); on press, computed transform, background-color and border-color are byte-identical to hover. This is the same mechanism the file's own comments record twice (':290 — a clip-path keyframe with fill:both outranks any plain author declaration'; the r1 fix of record-tag-never-paints) and it has come back on the one interactive region on the screen. The gate does not see it: interaction-check.mjs:1313-1325 proves the press by string-matching 'a.kpi:active' in document.styleSheets, so 'every control acknowledges a press' passes on a rule that has never painted — L-06, a gate that has never failed.
confirmed.consequence: Hovering the card that names the reader's biggest problem — '3 haven't moved in a fortnight' — produces a hairline going from 4% to 7% ink and nothing else, so the card reads as a static tile rather than something you can act on. Pressing it produces no acknowledgement at all. On a phone, where the gate's own comment says a press is the only channel that can confirm a touch landed, tapping the card gives the reader nothing: the tap leaves the card in its hover border and no press moment ever happens. Every state this row declares is decoration in the source and absent on screen.
confirmed.fix: The seat's fix works as measured, but it buys with JS what one CSS word buys outright. Prefer: at lately.html:485 change `.rise { animation: rise 0.5s var(--ease) both; ... }` to `... backwards; ...`. rise's `to` frame (opacity 1, transform none) is byte-identical to the element's natural resting state, so dropping only the forwards half changes no pixel of the entrance, keeps the backwards half that hides the element during its stagger delay, and releases transform back to the author cascade the instant the run ends. Measured in the same harness: hover matrix(1,0,0,1,0,-2), press background rgb(244,244,245), border rgb(161,161,170), identical in settled, play and reduced-motion, with the class still on all eleven elements. It needs no per-render wiring, and it cannot be defeated by a descendant's animationend bubbling into a `{ once: true }` listener and consuming it before the element's own event arrives - a hazard the seat's version only escapes by timing luck (.record-tag at :290 runs a keyframe literally named `rise` inside .card.hero.rise, and only its 1.5s delay keeps it from racing the hero's own 565ms end). Keep the second half of the seat's fix verbatim: replace :325 with `a.kpi:active { transform: translateY(0); background: var(--paper-3); border-color: var(--ink-4); }`. Then close the gate hole that let this through: interaction-check.mjs must stop proving the press by string-matching 'a.kpi:active' in document.styleSheets and instead hover the card with a real pointer, hold mouse-down, and assert that the computed transform/background/border triple differs from rest AND from hover - otherwise the identical class of bug re-enters on the next control.
confirmed.assertion: After settle, assert every element that carried .rise has computed animation-name 'none'. Then, in each of the three motion modes (default, ?motion=play, reducedMotion), move a real mouse onto a.kpi and assert its computed transform differs from its rest transform; hold pointerdown and assert at least one of transform, background-color or border-color differs from the hover state. Break the fix and watch each of the four fail first.

confirmed.element: .fortnight span ("A fortnight") in the ages strip, quiet state, all widths; worst at 390
confirmed.problem: The label is positioned `left: var(--gap-tight)` off a rule placed at `calc(var(--x) * 1%)` and never flips. In the quiet state the axis maximum derives to 15 and the fortnight sits at 93% of the strip, so the label runs off the right-hand end. Driven: at 1440 and 1280 it overhangs the strip by 24px and stops exactly on the card's border (label right 1289, card right 1290) with none of the 24px padding every other element in that card respects; at 768 it clears the card by 30px; at 390 it clears the card by 55px, is painted on the page ground outside the white card, and is then guillotined by .scroll's `overflow-x: hidden` - the phone shows "A FORTN". Two gate rules look adjacent to this and neither covers it: "no chart label leaves its card" reads the week chart, "no age tick leaves the strip" reads `.strip-scale`. This is not a fixture edge - it triggers whenever the oldest open job is near a fortnight, which is the ordinary case the strip is built to show.
confirmed.consequence: In the state where the owner is being told everything is fine, the single mark that gives the strip its meaning - the line that separates recent from sitting - is unnamed on a phone. The reader sees a dashed vertical rule near the right edge and a clipped word floating outside the card, and has to guess whether it is the threshold, the axis end, or a rendering fault. It also breaks the card's own margin at desk width, where the label is the only thing on the surface touching a border.
confirmed.fix: Take the fix as proposed and add two things it leaves out. (1) Reset before measuring, the pattern measureReading already uses at lately.html:1057-1062: inside relayout(), f.removeAttribute('data-flip'); then measure span.getBoundingClientRect().right against strip.getBoundingClientRect().right + 0.5 and re-set it. As written the attribute is only ever added, so once a resize flips the label it stays flipped at widths where it would fit — invisible on the shipped fixtures (in quiet the flip is needed at every strip width up to 1372px, and in full it is needed below 133px, so neither crosses the boundary) but live the moment a derived axis lands mid-range, e.g. oldest 17 gives axisMax 20 and a rule at 70%, which needs the flip below a 305px strip and not above it. (2) Guard the flipped side too — clamp so a flipped label cannot pass strip.left — even though no current axis can put the rule far enough left to trigger the flip and far enough left to overrun, because the whole class of defect here is an anchor with only one bound. Order matters: run it inside the existing relayout(), after deswarm(), so it re-runs on fonts.ready and on resize; the label's width is font-dependent (83.5px in Geist Mono, different in the fallback face) and a measurement taken against the fallback is a measurement of a page nobody sees. Then close the gate that let this through: widen interaction-check.mjs:884 from '.strip-scale span' to '.strip-scale span, .fortnight span' so the assertion becomes 'nothing in the strip leaves the strip', and assert .scroll.scrollWidth <= .scroll.clientWidth + 1 alongside the documentElement check at :88-91, since the document-level test is blind to anything .scroll clips.
confirmed.assertion: For every state and every declared viewport, in both grounds: `.fortnight span`'s bounding box is fully contained by `.strip`'s bounding box (left >= strip.left and right <= strip.right), and its text is never visually clipped (scrollWidth <= clientWidth + 1).
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed, and the numbers hold to a decimal. Driven in chromium at ?v=light&state=quiet across 1440/1280/768/390 with the entrance settled. Mechanism as described: lately.html:374-375 anchors .fortnight at left: calc(var(--x) * 1%) inside .strip and hangs its label at left: var(--gap-tight) with white-space: nowrap and no counter-anchor, and nothing in the relayout pass (lately.html:1038-1069) touches it. The quiet scope's oldest job is 12 (fixture.js), so D.axisMax = max(5, ceil(14/5)*5) = 15 (lately.html:617) and D.fortnight = 14 puts the rule at 93.333% of the strip. Measured, label box 83.5px wide in Geist Mono uppercase: 1440 — strip right 1265, label right 1288.6, card right 1290, so it overhangs the strip by 23.6px and stops 1.4px short of the card's own border with none of the 24px padding every sibling respects; 1280 — identical, label right 1208.6 against card right 1210; 768 — label right 749.8 against card right 720, so 29.8px of it is painted on the page ground outside the white card; 390 — label 337.5 to 421.0 against card right 366 and viewport 390, so it clears the card by 55px and is then guillotined by .scroll's overflow-x: hidden (.scroll scrollWidth 421 vs clientWidth 390). The screenshot at 390 reads exactly 'A FORTN', floating off the card. This is not a fixture edge: the escape triggers whenever the oldest open job is close to a fortnight, which is the state the strip exists to reassure about. The two adjacent gate rules do miss it, verified in source: interaction-check.mjs:627 collects only '.plot .gridline b, .plot .record-tag, .plot .bar-val' and tests them against '.card.hero' (:644), and :867 collects only '.strip-scale span' (:884). The universal 'no sideways scroll' floor (:88-91) reads documentElement.scrollWidth, which is 390 at 390 precisely because .scroll clips first, and 'no silent text clipping' (:134-153) skips .scroll because it holds no direct text node. So the surface is 421px wide inside a 390px clip and every gate is green. Not a re-file of fortnight-marker-lands-beside-a-fifteen-day-tick (r1): that claim was about the rule being mistaken for a 15d tick and was killed on the consequence; this is the label's box leaving its container, a different mechanism with a measured overflow. Note for the record that the r1 refuter's own sharpenedFix proposed right-anchoring this label and only the .strip-scale half of it shipped, so the anchor was left open by an accident of scope, not by decision. Severity: the seat's 'defect' is the right class and I would not raise it. The threshold's meaning survives elsewhere — .dot.old paints accent past the line, the KPI card counts it, and the sr paragraph states it — so the product asserts nothing untrue; it is visibly wrong and passable, not misleading. Testing against the strip's box is exactly correct rather than the card's, because the strip's left/right edges already sit on the card's content box (231/1265 against a card of 206/1290 with 24px padding and a 1px border). It needs two lines it does not state, given in sharpenedFix; that is a sharpening, not a correction, so this confirms.

What it can break: (a) the flipped label sits on the same top:0 row as nothing else today, but it now occupies the 84px immediately left of the rule, which is where a dot would sit for an age of roughly axisMax minus four days; the dots are 32px lower in a 92px strip so they do not collide at any width I measured, but deswarm() raises the strip's min-height by 20px per extra row and a dense strip pushes rows upward toward the label, so re-run the collision check at maximum swarm; (b) tooltips are position:fixed off the dot, unaffected; (c) the loading state hides .fortnight with visibility:hidden (lately.html:460), which still returns a real rect, so the measurement is valid there — confirm it does not throw when .fortnight is absent, which it is on first-run, empty and error (D.showsFortnight is false), so guard the querySelector. confirmed.element: .xaxis on the first-run chart (.plot.solo), all widths
confirmed.problem: `.plot.solo` narrows `.cols` and `.baseline` to 57px and re-anchors `.bar-val`, but `.xaxis` is untouched: it keeps `justify-content: space-between` and its single `span` keeps `flex: 1 1 0; text-align: center`, so the one date label centres itself in the whole chart column. Driven at ?state=first-run: the column's centre is 608 and the label's centre is 905 - the only date on the chart stands 298px to the right of the only mark it names (298px at 1280, 238px at 768, 109px at 390). The same layout leaves 631px of the hero card's 688px evidence column empty at 1440, so a reader's eye crosses two-thirds of a card of white to reach a date that belongs to a column behind them.
confirmed.consequence: A new owner's first chart reads as broken. There is a hatched bar at the far left and a date floating in the middle of a white field with nothing under it, so the two objects that should be one fact do not look related - and the reader cannot tell whether the date names the bar, names something that failed to draw, or names the empty space itself. This is the state that has to earn the surface's credibility, and it is the state where the layout most obviously has not been composed.
confirmed.fix: One rule, no grid change, no span change: `.plot.solo ~ .xaxis { width: 57px; padding-right: 0; }`. The existing span keeps `flex: 1 1 0; text-align: center` and fills the 57px box, centring the tick on the 57px .cols track. Measured injected: text centre 607.5 vs bar centre 607.5 at 1440 and 69.5 vs 69.5 at 390 - delta 0.0 at every width, versus -5.7 for the seat's version and +297.5 today. The `~` combinator is valid here (.xaxis is a following sibling of .plot.solo inside .chart) and reaches no other axis, so the twelve-column charts in movement one and the age axis are untouched. Leave .chart and .hero alone: the empty right-hand field is the drawn-but-empty consequence of one week of data, and it is the correct place for the slack once the tick stands on its mark - the text column is capped at 300px/30ch and cannot absorb it, so any width surgery only relocates the emptiness while risking the 768/390 stack.
confirmed.assertion: For state=first-run at every declared viewport: |centre(.xaxis span) - centre(.plot.solo .colw)| <= 4px, and the `.chart` element's width is within 8px of the `.plot.solo .cols` width.
confirmed.verdict: problem affirmed, seat's fix replaced — The problem is real and the measurements are right; the proposed fix is wrong in both halves, and one half is actively harmful, so this is refuted as filed under the rule that a correct problem with a wrong fix is refuted with the corrected fix returned. PROBLEM, verified: lately.html:275-277 narrows .cols and .baseline to 57px and re-anchors .bar-val for .plot.solo, but leaves .xaxis (line 295, justify-content: space-between, padding-right: var(--gutter) 34px) and its span (line 296, flex: 1 1 0; text-align: center) untouched. The :only-child guard at lines 304-307 means the 560-900px tick-thinning rules never apply to the solo axis, so the single span stretches the full 652px and centres its text in the whole chart column. Driven in chromium at ?state=first-run, text centre measured with a Range against the bar's box centre: 1440 bar.cx 607.5 / text 905.0 = 297.5px; 1280 bar.cx 527.5 / text 825.0 = 297.5px; 768 157.5 / 395.0 = 237.5px; 390 69.5 / 178.0 = 108.5px. The seat's 298/238/109 are right; its '608 and 905' pair is the 1440 reading, not the 1280 one, and the dead width is 629px of a 686px track, not 631 of 688 — both immaterial. light-first-run--1440x960.png confirms the perceptual claim: a hatched column with '12 SO FAR' at the far left of the evidence field and '13 JUL' alone in open paper two-thirds of the way across, sitting over nothing. Class defect is correct: the axis is aria-hidden and the sr line at lately.html:953 carries the full spoken fact, so nothing untrue is asserted and no reader is misinformed - it is visibly uncomposed, not misleading. FIX, refuted: (1) '.chart:has(.plot.solo) { flex: 0 0 auto; align-self: start; }' is inert. .chart is a grid item of .hero (line 219, grid-template-columns: minmax(220px,300px) 1fr), not a flex item, so flex is ignored and align-self only touches the block axis. Injected and measured: chart.w stays 686, computed grid stays '300px 686px', card height stays 268.9 - a dead rule, and lessons.md already carries dead-rules as a found-and-fixed class. (2) The parenthetical alternative is worse than inert. 'minmax(220px, 300px) auto' still stretches the auto track under normal justify-content: injected at 1440 the chart stayed 686px and the label stayed at 905, delta unchanged at 297.5. At 390 the :has() override out-specifies the stacking rule at line 514 (.hero { grid-template-columns: 1fr }) and reinstates two columns: hero-fig 252px, chart 32px, the bar thrown to cx 345.5 and clipped. That is a mobile-layout break traded for a desktop no-op. (3) The rationale is false. 'the hero's text column takes the slack' cannot happen: the first track is hard-capped at 300px by minmax() and .hero-note is max-width: 30ch (line 229). fig.w measured 300px in every variant that rendered. Narrowing the chart only moves 629px of dead width from the middle of the card to its right edge. (4) The span override introduces a fresh error. With .xaxis at width 57px and the span at 'flex: 0 0 auto', space-between packs the shrunk ~34px span to flex-start, so the label lands 5.7px LEFT of the column centre at every width - measured delta -5.7 at both 1440 and 390. The span's existing 'flex: 1 1 0; text-align: center' is what makes it land exactly; the seat proposed removing the one declaration that was already correct.

confirmed.element: .dot focus behaviour at 1440x960, the frame width this surface is shot and graded at
confirmed.problem: `.dot` carries no `scroll-margin`, so focusing the first mark scrolls the container the bare minimum. confirmed.consequence: A keyboard user arrives at the ages strip and finds a 12px dot pinned to the bottom edge of the screen with its ring cut off, no ruler underneath it, and no way to tell 2 days from 41 days except by reading nine tooltips one at a time. confirmed.fix: Ship it as written - `.dot { scroll-margin-bottom: var(--gap-hall); scroll-margin-top: var(--gap-room); }` - with one honest note on the second value: it is inert at the graded frame. Keep it anyway - it is the symmetric guard for the taller scroll ranges (390 has 1820px of travel) and it costs nothing - but the bottom value is the one doing the work, and 48 is load-bearing: 24 does not clear the card.

confirmed.element: The scroll container — .scroll (lately.html:171), inside .canvas (:170) and .app (:153), with html, body { height: 100% } (:116)

confirmed.verdict: problem affirmed, seat's fix replaced — The mechanism is real; two of the finding's load-bearing perceptual claims are measurably false, and the fix as written turns a green gate red. Confirmed: kpi() at lately.html:692-694 does split on `known && n > 0`; in full the row is DIV(9 lead), A(3), A(2), A(1), DIV(0) — three anchors at href='#', tabIndex 0, cursor pointer; partial is A(3), DIV(—), A(1), DIV(0); first-run inverts to one anchor among four divs, as claimed. Refuted on the two claims the consequence actually rests on. FIRST, 'At rest the two are pixel-identical — same paper, same hairline, same 34px numeral, same meter' is wrong on the meter, and the meter is the element that decides it. Measured on a 170px track: the three anchors paint indigo #4f46e5 at 57 / 38 / 19px (scaleX 0.333 / 0.222 / 0.111); the zero card paints 0px on a zinc-300 rail (.meter i.zero, --f:0); the unavailable card in partial draws no meter at all and prints 'Not available'. The link/div split is tracked exactly by the meter in every state — an anchor always carries paint in that slot, a div never does. A filled meter does not *announce* a link role, and I am not pretending it does, but the row is not the undifferentiated wall of five identical tiles the finding describes, and the sentence 'nothing at rest to tell them apart' is false as written. SECOND, the finding credits the anchors with 'its own hover and active rules' and then builds the fix on deleting them. Measured, that transform channel is already dead: .rise (:485) is `animation: rise 0.5s var(--ease) both` and @keyframes rise (:480) ends `to { transform: none }`, so the filled animation value outranks every normal declaration and pins transform on all five cards forever. THIRD, and decisive under this file's rule that a correct problem with a wrong fix is refuted: dropping the anchor branch as proposed makes `has('a.kpi:active')` false, so interaction-check.mjs:1325 'every control acknowledges a press' fails and the behaviour gate goes 365/366. confirmed.element: The resize handler (lately.html:1072) — `window.addEventListener("resize", () => { relayout(); queueMove(); })`
confirmed.problem: The handler re-runs the de-swarm and the reading-line measurement and repositions the tooltip, but it never puts the focused element back on screen. Driven at 1440x960: focus the fifth mark, tip up and correctly placed 8px above it, then resize to 1280x844 — the mark is now at top 948 in an 844px window, 104px below the fold; at 768 it is at 1,457; at 390 it is at 1,570, 726px below the fold. In each case document.activeElement is still that mark and the tooltip has correctly hidden itself (onMove sees the mark out of view), so the reader is left with no visible focus ring anywhere on the screen and no label. This is the class the defect library names outright — 'Focus that leaves the screen: keep the focused element scrolled into view through every move' — creeping back through the one repaint path the surface has.
confirmed.consequence: A keyboard or screen-magnifier reader loses their place on a rotation or a window resize. The ring is gone from the screen, the mark's title — which lives nowhere else on this surface — is gone with it, and the only way back is to press Tab and land somewhere else entirely. On a phone, rotating to landscape and back is a routine gesture, and it costs the reader the position they had worked to reach.
confirmed.fix: Take the seat's handler as written, with one addition. block: "nearest" parks the mark flush against the viewport bottom -- measured at 1280x844 and 390x844 the restored mark sits at top 832, bottom 844 -- and .dot:focus-visible is a 2px outline at outline-offset: 3px, so the bottom 5px of the ring is clipped off-screen. Add `scroll-margin-block: 12px` to the `.dot` rule (lately.html:348) so "nearest" leaves room for the ring; that also improves the browser's own tab-arrival scroll, which produces the same knife-edge today (948/960 at 1440x960) and is the state this whole finding starts from. Do not switch to block: "center" -- it yanks the reader further than the move that displaced them. Final handler at :1072: window.addEventListener("resize", () => { const held = document.activeElement; relayout(); if (held && held !== document.body && root.contains(held)) { const b = held.getBoundingClientRect(); if (b.top < 0 || b.bottom > window.innerHeight) held.scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest" }); } queueMove(); });

Repeat with a focused KPI card. Watch the 1280 step fail against the current file (top 948 in an 844px window).

Chromium, ?v=light&state=full, 1440x960: seven Tabs reach the strip, four more land on the fifth mark, and the browser's own minimal scroll-into-view parks it flush at the fold (top 948, bottom 960, .scroll scrollTop 4) with the tip on. Resize with nothing else touched: 1280x844 leaves the mark at top 948 in an 844 window (104px below), 768x1024 at 1457 (433px below, in a viewport TALLER than the one it was focused in, so this is content reflow, not window shrink), 390x844 at 1570 (726px below). In all three document.activeElement is still that mark, tip.classList 'on' is gone, scrollTop never moves off 4. The behaviour gate never resizes with focus held, so this is not a restatement of it; the class is named in the defect library at lessons.md:265 and it is back through the one path the surface has. What does reproduce is the arrival state -- the first Tab onto the strip always leaves the mark knife-edged at the fold, and any resize from there strands it -- which is common enough to carry the finding without the rotation claim. The fix is correct as written: root is in scope at :1072, .scroll has no scroll-behavior: smooth so scrollIntoView lands instantly, and the seat's claim about ordering holds -- onMove does not clear `showing` on the out-of-view branch, so the queueMove rAF fires after the scroll and re-places the tip against the restored position. confirmed.element: .xaxis span in the twelve-week chart, in the two thinned bands (max-width 1140 and min-width 901; and max-width 792)
confirmed.problem: At full density the twelve spans are `flex: 1 1 0`, so each label centres on its own column. In the thinned bands the media query switches the three survivors to `flex: 0 0 auto` inside a `space-between` row, so they are distributed by the container instead of standing on their values. Driven, offset of a tick's centre from its column's centre: at 1140 "8 Jun" is 23px left of column 7 against a 49px column pitch; at 792, 23px; at 768, 22px against a 47px pitch; at 390 all three are off - "27 Apr" +13, "8 Jun" -12, "13 Jul" -13 against a 25.7px pitch, i.e. every visible label on the phone is displaced by half a column and centres on the gap between two bars. This is the mechanism the panel already killed on the age axis in round 1 (ticks stand on their values rather than being spread by flexbox); it survives untouched on the week axis.
confirmed.consequence: On a phone the label naming the running week - the one column the reader is looking for - sits over the boundary between the last two columns, so the finished 6 Jul week and the unfinished 13 Jul week are equally plausible readings of it. In the 1024-1140 band and at 768 the mid-chart label lands nearly half a column away, so a reader pinning a date to a bar picks the wrong bar or gives up and reads shape only. The chart's whole claim is that twelve specific weeks are drawn; three labels that do not stand on the weeks they name withdraw it at three of the four widths this ships at.

Making the survivor a flex container turns its text into an anonymous flex item whose automatic minimum size is the nowrap text, so justify-content:center overflows it symmetrically instead of flushing it left, and the ink centres on the box - which, at flex:1 1 0, IS the column. Driven in chromium at ?v=light&state=full, reading each tick's ink box (Range.getBoundingClientRect) against its own .colw centre: at 1440 and at 900/860 all twelve spans are flex:1 1 0 and every visible tick is 0.0px off its column. At 390 '27 Apr' is nearer column 2's centre (10.0px) than column 1's (13.2px), '13 Jul' is nearer column 11 (10.0px) than column 12 (13.2px), and '8 Jun' sits dead on the col6/col7 boundary. So the mechanism the panel killed on the age axis in r1 does survive on the week axis, the behaviour gate does not cover it (interaction-check.mjs:735-754 asserts only one-line-ness and in-card containment for .xaxis; the alignment assertion at :856-885 is scoped to .strip-scale), and this is not a re-file of any closed or refuted item. The seat's own denominators are wrong in the conservative direction - 49px, 47px and 25.7px against measured 46.67, 44.67 and 23.17 - so the true fraction of a pitch is worse than claimed, not better; the offsets themselves are right within 1.6px. What refutes it is the prescription. I applied the seat's exact rule (display:none -> visibility:hidden on the non-survivors, display:block; flex:0 0 auto -> visibility:visible on 1st/7th/last, flex basis left alone) and re-measured. It fixes 1140/792/768, where the box is wider than the label. It does not fix the phone, which is the width the seat calls the damage: at 390 the boxes resolve to 19.17px against 45.5px of nowrap text, and chromium flushes an overflowing line to the start edge rather than centring it, so the ink lands +13.2 / +9.4 / +13.2 - '27 Apr' unchanged, '8 Jun' still 0.41 of a pitch out, and '13 Jul' flipped from -13.2 to +13.2, now sitting past the last column instead of on the boundary before it. Every visible label on the phone is still displaced by roughly half a column after the fix that was sold as removing exactly that. A correct problem with a fix that leaves its own worst case standing is refuted; the corrected one-declaration version is below.

confirmed.element: ICON.nobody, the square glyph on the "has nobody's name on it" card, ?v=dark
confirmed.problem: The four status glyphs hard-code their hues in the SVG strings (`stroke="#4f46e5"` and the rest), so they alone do not take part in the ground flip. The dark twin exists in part because Indigo 600 on a near-black ground reads as a bruise, and steps `--accent` to Indigo 400 - every other indigo mark on the surface (the live column, the meter fills, the old dots, the focus ring, the bar value) takes that step; the status square does not. Measured against the plate it actually paints on (`--wash` over `--paper`, #202023): the indigo square renders at 2.58:1, below the 3:1 floor for a mark that carries meaning, while its three neighbours sit at 5.6, 4.7 and 4.7. The audit gate reads text colour against the composited backdrop and does not walk SVG stroke attributes, so nothing sees it.
confirmed.consequence: On the dark ground one of the four status categories loses its mark: the square is barely separable from its own plate, so a row that should read as four distinct kinds of slippage reads as three plus a blank. The file's stated rule is that status wears a shape as well as a colour and never a colour alone - here it wears a shape nobody can see, which is the same failure from the other end.
confirmed.fix: Take the proposed fix with one addition it omits. ICON.clear (lately.html:649) is a fifth glyph in the same object, rendered into a bare .glyph in the quiet state at line 924. If it is converted to currentColor along with its four siblings but its wrapper is not given a tone, it inherits color from the card — #ffffff in dark — and the emerald tick silently becomes a white tick. So either leave clear hard-coded (works, but leaves the file with two conventions for one object) or, better, convert all five and give the quiet card's glyph the emerald tone too. Plumbing: kpi() takes glyph as an opaque HTML string, so pass a tone alongside it and emit style="color:var(--amber|--red|--accent|--emerald)" on the span; do not add a new token — all four already exist and only --accent is redefined in dark, which is precisely the one that should move. While in here, note a separate defect the fix will put you nose-to-nose with and should not silently fix: the comment at lately.html:642-644 states the order is 'amber, indigo, red, emerald ... because red adjacent to amber fails CVD separation at 4.4', but the row is rendered still/past/nobody/waiting at lines 813-816, i.e. amber, red, indigo, emerald — red IS adjacent to amber. The code and its own stated CVD rationale disagree. That belongs in its own finding.
confirmed.assertion: For state=full at ?v=dark: every `.kpi .glyph svg [stroke]` resolves to a colour whose contrast against the composited background of its `.glyph` is >= 3.0:1, and no SVG on the surface carries a literal hex stroke that differs from the value the same token resolves to in the current ground.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed by driving ?v=dark&state=full in chromium at 1440x960 and reading computed style off the live nodes. The mechanism is exactly as described: lately.html:645-649 hard-codes stroke="#d97706" / "#ef4444" / "#4f46e5" / "#059669" on the four status glyphs, while ICON.up and ICON.down two lines above (640-641) already use stroke="currentColor" — so the file contains both patterns and the status four are the ones that missed. In dark the four .kpi .glyph shapes computed to rgb(217,119,6), rgb(239,68,68), rgb(79,70,229), rgb(5,150,105) — byte-identical to light, confirming they do not take the ground flip, while --accent resolves to #818cf8 and every other indigo mark on the surface (12 var(--accent) uses: live column, meter fills, hatch, dots, focus ring) does. The plate is real: .glyph background is --wash = rgba(255,255,255,0.04) over .kpi background --paper = rgb(24,24,27), compositing to #212124 (the finding says #202023; one rounding step off, immaterial). Indigo 600 on that plate is 2.55:1 — the finding's 2.58 is what you get on #202023, so its own number is right to two figures — against a 3:1 floor for a meaning-carrying mark. The sharpest version of the claim is one the seat only implies: in that same card the meter directly beneath the square computes to rgb(129,140,248), so the 'has nobody's name on it' card paints Indigo 600 and Indigo 400 forty pixels apart, in a twin whose written rule (lately.html:86-90) is that indigo steps to 400 because 600 on near-black reads as a bruise. That is a self-contradiction in the file, measured, not taste. The gate claim is right in effect and imprecise in mechanism: audit.mjs DOES walk fill/stroke — colorProps at line 200 includes both and paints() at 197 gates them on el.matches(SHAPES) — but only for the palette lock; the contrast block fires solely on hasText/::placeholder, so no non-text mark on this surface is contrast-checked. Nothing sees it, for a different reason than stated. Two corrections that do not change the verdict. (1) The neighbour ratios 5.6/4.7/4.7 are measured against #18181b, not against the wash plate the finding itself argues is the right backdrop; on that plate they are 5.04/4.27/4.27. The outlier gap holds either way. (2) 'a row that should read as four distinct kinds of slippage reads as three plus a blank' is overstated — captured at deviceScaleFactor 3 and compared against a patched twin, the square is plainly visible, just muddier and a step darker than every other indigo on the page. Defect is the right class and I am keeping it: visibly wrong, passable, nothing asserted untrue and nothing broken. The proposed fix is mechanically correct and I verified it: setting color on .glyph and stroke="currentColor" on the shapes moved the square to rgb(129,140,248) (5.38:1 on the plate) and left the amber circle at rgb(217,119,6) untouched. Light is a genuine no-op because --accent is #4f46e5 in :root and --amber/--red/--emerald carry no dark override at all. No new hue, no new weight, no architecture touched.

confirmed.element: --mark-ctx at lately.html:41 (light) and :100 (dark), as painted by .bar at :239 and .dot::before at :357
confirmed.problem: Composited and measured at 1440 in both grounds: the eleven history columns and the six inside-a-fortnight age dots resolve to #d4d4d8 on #ffffff - 1.48:1 - in light, and #3f3f46 on #18181b - 1.70:1 - in dark. WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of graphical objects required to understand the content, and these are not decoration around the content, they are the content: the twelve-week shape and the nine-mark age distribution. The essential-presentation exception does not reach them, because the lock contains darker zincs that would carry the same reading. Both gates are blind here by construction: audit.mjs's contrast pass reads size, weight and text and only ever judges type (scripts/audit.mjs:244 and :363), and the behaviour gate has no non-text rule at all. For scale, the same measurement puts the live indigo column at 6.29:1 light and 5.94:1 dark, so the surface is carrying a fourfold contrast gap between the mark it wants read and the eleven marks it needs read.
confirmed.consequence: The dark twin is the clearest case: the ages card states nine open jobs and, to anyone with reduced contrast sensitivity, shows three - the three indigo ones past the fortnight - because the other six sit at 1.70:1 on the ground. The reader is then answering "am I on top of this" from a third of the evidence, with no way of knowing marks are missing. In light the twelve-week chart degrades the same way: one indigo column and eleven that fade out in daylight or on a dimmed laptop.
confirmed.fix: Keep the token -- --mark-quiet: #71717a in :root and in [data-v="dark"] is right, Ink 3 is in the locked eighteen and clears 3:1 in both grounds (4.83:1 / 3.67:1) -- then spend it differently. (1) STRIP, form not density: leave the six recent dots the quieter mark but carry the floor on a ring instead of a fill -- .dot::before { background: transparent; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--disc); } with .dot { --disc: var(--mark-quiet) } and .dot.old::before { background: var(--disc) } restoring the solid fill at var(--accent). The 2px ring is the graphical object and clears 3:1; solid-versus-hollow is a fill difference, which is what the constraint sanctions, and it survives both CVD and reduced contrast sensitivity where a 1.30:1 luminance step does not. Re-point .dot:hover, .dot:focus-visible (:369) and .dot:active (:372) so they change the ring on a hollow dot rather than filling it, and leave .sk-wrap .dot::before (:457) its solid --wash so the loading state keeps its marks. (2) CHART, both marks or neither: do not repoint .bar on its own. If the eleven columns go to --mark-quiet, the current week must come with them -- raise the hatch to var(--accent) 0 3px, transparent 3px 6px in both .bar.part (:255) and the dark override (:263), keep the open top and the 1px accent rails, then re-measure the composited mean and confirm the current week still reads as the chart's dominant mark. It will not: a hatch over paper tops out near 1.73:1 whatever the duty cycle, so the honest conclusion is that the chart's compliance cannot be won by darkening the columns alone. Either give .bar.part a solid 1px Indigo 600/400 outline on left, right and bottom so the live week carries a 6.29:1 boundary as a delineated shape, or leave the columns at Ink 5 and argue the chart's case on its baseline, three valued gridlines and twelve dated ticks -- a weaker argument, but one the seat should make explicitly rather than assume. (3) Include .meter i.zero (:339) in whatever lands; it is the same mark at the same ratio. (4) Separately: .bar.live (:242) is dead in all seven states -- worth deleting, but that is the already-refuted dead-rules class, not this finding.
confirmed.assertion: Sample the composited fill of every .bar, every .dot::before and every .meter i against its composited backdrop, in both grounds and at 390/768/1280/1440, and require every one of them to reach 3:1. Wire it into audit.mjs as a non-text pass so it runs on every viewport the config declares.
confirmed.verdict: problem affirmed, seat's fix replaced — The measurement of the quiet marks is right and the load-bearing comparison built on top of it is wrong, and the fix inherits the error. Verified in chromium at 1440 in both grounds: --mark-ctx is #d4d4d8 at :41 and #3f3f46 at :100, .bar at :241 and .dot::before at :357 paint exactly those, the ground under both is var(--paper) = #ffffff / #18181b, eleven of twelve columns carry class "bar" and six of nine dots carry no .old, and the ratios are 1.48:1 and 1.70:1 as claimed. Both gates are blind as claimed: audit.mjs's contrast pass is gated on hasText && visible and never reaches a fill, and interaction-check.mjs has no non-text rule at all (its only contrast assertion is the lead-plate numeral at :1175). So far the seat is correct. WHAT IS WRONG: the finding's scale argument -- "the live indigo column at 6.29:1 light and 5.94:1 dark, so the surface is carrying a fourfold contrast gap" -- measures .bar.live, and .bar.live paints in ZERO states. Driven across all seven (full, partial, quiet, first-run, empty, loading, error) the count of .bar.live is 0 every time, because chart() at :714 reads w.partial ? "bar part" : (live ? "bar live" : "bar") and the twelfth week is partial:true in the fixture for every scope. The mark that actually paints is .bar.part: hatched Indigo at a 2-in-6 duty cycle over transparent with the top 28% masked, which composites -- element screenshot, mean over the drawn box -- to rgb(195.5,192.5,246.0) = 1.71:1 on #ffffff and rgb(59.6,63.3,101.6) = 1.77:1 on #18181b. Against the eleven context columns that is a gap of 1.18:1 in light and 1.07:1 in dark, not fourfold. The current week's column is not the compliant mark the finding contrasts against the failing ones; by the finding's own 1.4.11 standard it is the worst offender on the chart, and the finding never sees it. THE FIX THEREFORE FAILS ITS OWN TEST AND INVERTS THE CHART. Applied as written and re-measured: the eleven history columns rise to 4.40:1 composited in light and 3.45:1 in dark (pure swatch 4.83:1 / 3.67:1 -- the finding's 3.68 is a rounding, not an error), while the one mark the whole surface is built around stays at 1.71:1 / 1.77:1, still under the floor. Visually the result is eleven heavy zinc-500 blocks with the running week as the faintest, most fragile thing in the frame -- context-versus-live flips from 1.18:1 to 2.56:1 in light and 1.07:1 to 1.95:1 in dark, with the darker mark now on the wrong side. The fix's stated justification, "the live column is darker (6.29:1), it is indigo, and it is hatched", is false on its first clause and internally inconsistent with its third: a hatch over paper cannot be 6.29:1, and this one is not. ON THE STRIP THE FIX MAKES THE READING WORSE. Repointing --disc flat drops the achromatic separation between past-a-fortnight and recent from 4.25:1 to 1.30:1 in light and from 3.50:1 to 1.62:1 in dark, leaving the strip's only real reading -- three jobs are sitting -- carried by hue alone. That is the one thing the palette lock names as forbidden: status and hierarchy are expressed by ink density, weight and fill, not by colour. The finding buys 1.4.11 on the six quiet dots by spending the CVD separation on the three that matter. The fix is also under-scoped: .meter i.zero at :339 is the same class of mark at the same 1.48:1 / 1.70:1 and is left alone, and it is the only mark in three of the first-run KPI cards; and in ?state=quiet the .dot.old count is 0, so all nine dots are quiet marks and no indigo appears in the strip at all -- a state the finding's consequence paragraph never reaches. Severity stands at defect for the underlying shortfall: the marks are visible to a normal-sighted reader at 1440, so visibly-wrong-but-passable is the right class -- but the seat's own case for it rests on a number that does not exist on this surface.
