confirmed.element: quiet state, the "Nothing is sitting" card's body sentence
confirmed.problem: The full state's band counts four conditions - hasn't moved in a fortnight, past the day it was due, nobody's name on it, waiting on something else. The quiet state replaces all four cards with one sentence, and the sentence names three: "All 9 open jobs have moved inside a fortnight, none is past its day, and every one has a name on it." The fourth, waiting on something else, is zero in the quiet scope and is simply not mentioned. The band's own principle is stated in the code beside it - the band does not vanish, because an absent band reads as a bug - and the same reasoning applies one level down, to a category that vanishes from the sentence that replaces it.
confirmed.consequence: An owner who has learned the four kinds of slippage from the full state reads the all-clear and finds only three of them cleared. The most natural reading of a missing item in a list of four is that it was not checked, which is the one impression this surface works hardest not to give.
confirmed.fix: Take the fix exactly as proposed, in the row's order: `${D.open === 1 ? "The one open job has" : `All ${D.open} open jobs have`} moved inside a fortnight, none is past its day, every one has a name on it, and none is waiting on anything else.` Two sharpenings. (1) Keep the row order even though it costs a widow - at 1440/768 line three renders as the single word 'else.' I measured two reorderings that put the waiting clause third ('...none is waiting on anything else, and every one has a name on it' and '...none is waiting on anything, and every one has a name on it') and both still widow ('on it.' / 'it.') while breaking the correspondence with the card order that is the whole point of the finding. The measure is 44ch; a short last line is inherent, not a reason to reorder. If the widow is worth removing, remove it with the wrap and not the words. (2) While this line is open, make the singular branch subject-consistent - as it stands D.open === 1 yields 'The one open job has moved inside a fortnight, none is past its day, every one has a name on it', which switches subject mid-sentence, and the fix inherits that. 'The one open job has moved inside a fortnight, is not past its day, has a name on it, and is not waiting on anything else' is the same four in the same order and reads. Note the branch is currently unreachable on this surface: D.open is bound to F.bound.openCount = 9 and derive-fixture.mjs fails the build if any scope carries a different count.
confirmed.assertion: For state=quiet: the `.center .t-body` sentence contains one clause for each of the four status keys in the scope (sitting, overdue, unowned, waiting), matched by the same phrase stems the KPI captions use.
confirmed.verdict: Every load-bearing claim checks out when driven. lately.html:812-816 builds the band from five cards - leadKpi (the shared 9) plus exactly four conditions in this order: hasn't moved in a fortnight, past the day it was due, nobody's name on it, waiting on something else. lately.html:926 replaces all five in the quiet state with one sentence that names three of the four: driven at file://...lately.html?v=light&state=quiet&motion=settled the card reads verbatim 'All 9 open jobs have moved inside a fortnight, none is past its day, and every one has a name on it.' I scanned the whole quiet DOM (main, not body, so the source template does not self-match): the string 'waiting' appears zero times anywhere on the rendered quiet page - not in the card, not in the band head, not in the ages card's spoken line, not in the coverage strip. In full it appears twice, as the fourth card's visible label and its sr line ('0 jobs are waiting on something else, of 9 jobs open'). derive-fixture.mjs:212 sets the quiet scope to sitting 0, overdue 0, unowned 0, waiting 0, so the fourth category is genuinely zero and genuinely unsaid. It is not a re-raise: quiet-state-contradicts-its-own-evidence (r1) was marks disagreeing with the sentence, and that is fixed - the quiet strip now tops out at 12 days under a 14-day rule and speaks '0 jobs have been open longer than a fortnight'. It is not a gate restatement either: the behaviour gate's quiet assertions only test /Nothing is sitting/ (interaction-check.mjs:807) and the fortnight card against the marks; no gate and no build step reads this sentence's wording. And it is not taste: the sentence has already committed to enumeration by naming three, so stopping one short is a list that comes up short, not a stylistic choice - and the state's own code comment two lines above states the governing principle ('the band does not vanish - an absent band reads as a bug'), which is exactly the reasoning one level down. The proposed fix is correct as written. I applied it live at 1440, 768 and 390 and re-measured: the body sits under .center .t-body max-width 44ch, so at 1440 and 768 the card grows from 2 lines to 3 - +23.25px, exactly one rung of the declared leading ladder, card 269.5px to 292.75px - and at 390 the card does not grow at all (the existing sentence already wraps to 3 lines there; the new clause fills the short third line, 292.75px before and after). Nothing else in the band moves, no gate reads the string, and no constraint is touched: this is copy only, no colour, no weight, no architecture. Severity is right at refinement and I am not correcting it upward: the sentence asserts nothing untrue, so it is not misleading, and the gap is invisible without cross-reading the full state, so it is not a defect. It is the last inch of an otherwise complete receipt.
confirmed.sharpenedFix: Take the fix exactly as proposed, in the row's order: `${D.open === 1 ? "The one open job has" : `All ${D.open} open jobs have`} moved inside a fortnight, none is past its day, every one has a name on it, and none is waiting on anything else.` Two sharpenings. (1) Keep the row order even though it costs a widow - at 1440/768 line three renders as the single word 'else.' I measured two reorderings that put the waiting clause third ('...none is waiting on anything else, and every one has a name on it' and '...none is waiting on anything, and every one has a name on it') and both still widow ('on it.' / 'it.') while breaking the correspondence with the card order that is the whole point of the finding. The measure is 44ch; a short last line is inherent, not a reason to reorder. If the widow is worth removing, remove it with the wrap and not the words. (2) While this line is open, make the singular branch subject-consistent - as it stands D.open === 1 yields 'The one open job has moved inside a fortnight, none is past its day, every one has a name on it', which switches subject mid-sentence, and the fix inherits that. 'The one open job has moved inside a fortnight, is not past its day, has a name on it, and is not waiting on anything else' is the same four in the same order and reads. Note the branch is currently unreachable on this surface: D.open is bound to F.bound.openCount = 9 and derive-fixture.mjs fails the build if any scope carries a different count.
confirmed.breaks: Nothing structural. The quiet card grows one line at 1440 and 768 (+23.25px, one leading rung; card 269.5 to 292.75px) and is unchanged at 390. Re-measure after it lands: the quiet frame in shots/light-quiet--1440x960.png must be recaptured (and dark, if the frame set carries it) since the card height changes; audit.mjs's leading and type-ramp checks over the taller .center block; and confirm the sentence still fits without a fourth line in dark and at 1280. The behaviour gate needs no edit - interaction-check.mjs:807 matches only /Nothing is sitting/ and nothing else asserts this copy - but this is the moment to add the assertion that is missing: for the quiet state, every non-zero-capable condition named in movementTwo's card set must appear in the all-clear sentence, so the next category added to the row cannot silently fall out of the sentence that replaces it. Watch also that the fourth clause is not written as a fact the fixture does not hold - it is true only because SCOPE.status.waiting is 0 for quiet, the same contract the other three clauses already ride on.

refuted.problem: The error state designs three of its four parts - the heading names the source, the sentence explains the refusal, the button offers the one move - and does not design the fourth. Driven: clicking #retry changes nothing measurable. The root's markup is identical before and after (3048 characters both times), the URL is unchanged, no live region fires, the console is silent, and the only difference is that the button now holds focus. There is no pending treatment, no disabled interval, no announcement, and no second state for "asked again, still nothing".
refuted.why: The headline is false and the fix is wrong about the source. (1) The title's claim is already closed and gate-proven. Driven in chromium at 1440 on ?v=light&state=error, holding the pointer down on #retry: background goes #ffffff -> rgb(244,244,245), border goes rgba(17,17,17,0.1) -> solid rgb(113,113,122), transform becomes matrix(1,0,0,1,0,1), el.matches(':active') true, over the declared 140ms curve (lately.html:440). That is a designed press. 'no-pressed-state-anywhere' was confirmed and fixed in r1 and interaction-check.mjs:1325 asserts '.btn:active' exists; the finding restates a gate assertion and re-raises a closed finding with no regression evidence. (2) The residue -- no in-flight treatment -- is not undesigned either. The pending treatment for this reading IS a designed state: `loading`, with skeletons at the real geometry of the sections that will render plus its own role=status 'Loading this reading.' line (lately.html:973-975). A retry re-enters that. The finding asks instead for a second, button-local pending vocabulary for the same wait. (3) The inertness is the master's declared position, not an oversight. Driven, every control on this surface is inert by construction: the three tabs are href='#', a.kpi is href='#' (l.693), the marks call preventDefault on click (l.1134), and 'Open Tasks' on the empty state leaves the DOM byte-identical exactly as #retry does. The round notes already state the rule -- 'The hero no longer says a finished job is openable, because nothing on this surface opens one. That is on the port packet, not on the screen.' Retry's wiring is the same class. (4) The proposed fix is factually wrong three times over. 'the button, the note block and the status line all exist' -- in the error state the only live region in the DOM is the role=alert wrapper (driven); there is no role=status element (loading's lives inside loading's own template), and a live region injected and populated in the same frame is unreliably announced, so the fix would ship an announcement that does not announce. There is no note block on the error card either: it is heading + paragraph + button, 3048 characters, nothing else. 'aria-disabled=true, pointer events off' would strand the ring on a dead control -- #retry is the only focusable thing in the error state's main (driven order: 3 tabs, then #retry) and aria-disabled leaves it in the tab order, so Enter still does nothing: the complaint reinstated, one indirection deeper. And 'Asked again at 09:16.' is a hand-typed wall clock on a surface whose only reading instant is the frozen fixture literal F.readingLong = '09:14, Thursday 16 July 2026' (fixture.js:27), printed by shell() in the same view twice (l.892, l.902) and declared bound in the coverage footer. Two clock times two minutes apart on a static frame with no elapsed time is the class that got 'error-state-invents-a-last-good-reading' and 'august-inside-a-july-reading' confirmed in r1; the fix would reopen both. (5) The severity is overstated. 'defect' means visibly wrong but passable; nothing in the error frame is visibly wrong. The ask is an eighth state plus live wiring on a master where nothing is wired, which is a build on the port packet, not a defect on the screen.

refuted.problem: On first-run the account is three days old (F.accountDays = 3) and the oldest open job is 3 days (scopes['first-run'].oldest). The surface knows this and acts on it in one place: D.showsFortnight resolves false, so the fortnight rule is deliberately not drawn on the strip, on the stated grounds that a rule no mark can reach reads as a rule every mark has beaten. Two hundred pixels above that suppressed rule the same threshold is printed as a result: a 34px "0" under the heading "What's quietly slipping", captioned "haven't moved in a fortnight", with a meter drawn against the shared denominator of 9. The identical argument applies and is not applied. The other three cards do not have this property - an overdue date or an unowned job can genuinely exist on day three, so their zeros are readings; this one is arithmetically forced.
refuted.why: Driven in chromium at 1440/1280/768/390 at ?state=first-run and read against lately.html and fixture.js. The mechanics check out: scopes['first-run'].oldest = 3, D.axisMax = max(5, ceil((3+2)/5)*5) = 5, D.showsFortnight = 14 <= 5 = false (no .fortnight node in the DOM at any width), and the sitting card renders 0 with .meter i.zero at scaleX(0) and speaks ' 0 jobs haven’t moved in a fortnight, of 9 jobs open'. Three things sink the finding anyway. (1) The class is overstated, and the brief makes an overstated class a reason to refute. misleading = the product asserts something untrue; every clause this card prints and speaks is true at the reading instant. The finding is an implicature argument, and the implicature is defeated inside the same section: the ages card’s own band-head prints OLDEST · 3 DAYS one rung below the row (measured gap 16px at 1440/1280/768/390), its scale runs today→5d, and the hero directly above prints 'jobs finished since you started' and 'Four weeks of records make a comparison worth printing. Yours arrive on 10 August 2026.' The context the fix wants to add is already on screen, 16px away, in a more precise form — the number 3 rather than the words 'that long'. Nothing is untrue and nothing is visibly wrong: refinement, and defect is the absolute ceiling. (2) It is not the identical argument. The suppressed rule is a drawn spatial comparison — a dashed line with nine dots ranged to its left, on an axis whose maximum the eye never reads — which manufactures the graphic of a field cleared. The card is a counted statement that carries its own denominator ('All five counted out of 9') and its own timescale in the caption. The surface already holds a designed position on genuine zeros and the behaviour gate encodes it at interaction-check.mjs:315, 'a true zero draws its meter and is not a link to an empty list'. This is a genuine zero, not the fabricated zero the honest-degradation contract forbids, so the contract is not being broken here. (3) The fix’s flag is the wrong flag, measured against the real source. D.showsFortnight is false exactly when D.axisMax < 14, i.e. when ceil((oldest+2)/5)*5 < 14, i.e. when oldest <= 8. The zero the finding calls arithmetically forced holds whenever oldest <= 13. Hooked to showsFortnight, the not-yet card silently stops firing for every account whose oldest job is 9 to 13 days old — five of the fourteen days it exists to cover, and the five nearest the threshold, where over-trusting the reading costs most (oldest 9–13 gives axisMax 15, showsFortnight true, plain 0 with a meter). showsFortnight is an axis-rendering artifact; the semantic condition is D.oldest < D.fortnight. On top of that the stated ground for dropping the meter inverts which term is frozen: 'a share of a denominator that cannot move' — but 9 open jobs moves every day; it is the numerator that is bounded. 0/9 is a true share of a live denominator, and dropping the meter pulls one of the five cards out of the comparable row on the one state where the shared denominator (a protected object) is the row’s whole argument. Measured cost of the label that would replace it, injected into the live page: at 390 'Nothing has been open that long yet' sets to three lines of tracked uppercase Geist Mono in a 131px content box, growing the card 157→198px and the row by 42px; at 1440 two lines, +7px. Correct problem framing, wrong fix and wrong class.

refuted.problem: D.open is F.bound.openCount, read unconditionally in the accessor and printed in every state. Driven at 1440 and read back: in `empty` the same strip says "TASKS ANSWERED, NOTHING RECORDED" and then "BOUND WORKSPACE, OWNER, READING DATE AND THE 9". In `error` it says "TASKS DID NOT ANSWER" and then the same 9. In `loading` it says all three sources are "READING" and still prints the 9. The open count is a Tasks-derived figure, so in two of those three the surface prints a number from a source it has just named as silent, one line away, in the same footer. This is not the closed error-state-invents-a-last-good-reading finding: the reading instant is a defensible stamp of when the attempt was made and I am not raising it. The open count is not - it is a reading, not an attempt.
refuted.why: The mechanism is real and the speech act is misread, which collapses the consequence. Driven in chromium at 1440 across all seven states with motion=settled: the footer does print BOUND WORKSPACE, OWNER, READING DATE AND THE 9 in every state, including empty, loading and error, and in empty and error no other 9 appears in main. But the stamp is not a reading of the current state - it is the lab's provenance disclosure. lately.html:903-904 sets the last two stamps as a pair, LAB counts and ages are lab-authored / BOUND workspace, owner, reading date and the 9, and fixture.js's generated header names exactly those four: 'Four facts are bound to src/lib/project-truth-fixture.ts and fail the build on drift: the reading date, the owner, the workspace name and the open-work denominator. Weekly completions, job ages and status counts are lab-authored.' The behaviour gate says the same thing in its own words at interaction-check.mjs:260-267, under the comment 'Provenance', asserting 'the surface says which of its numbers are lab-authored'. So the Bound stamp asserts 'the open-work denominator this lab is bound to is 9', a statement about the fixture binding that is true in all seven states, not 'you have 9 open jobs this morning'. Nothing untrue is asserted, so the honest-degradation contract - a missing source must not resolve to a fabricated number - is not touched: in empty and error the surface fabricates nothing in main, and the footer figure is the build-gated bound value, the opposite of a guess. The finding's own logic, applied evenly, would condemn its neighbour just as hard: LAB COUNTS AND AGES ARE LAB-AUTHORED also prints in empty and error where no count and no age is on screen. The seat does not raise it, because that stamp is plainly provenance - and so is the one beside it. Two load-bearing claims are also wrong when driven. (1) 'the denominator card is not on screen in any of those three states' - in loading it is on screen: VIEW.loading (lately.html:973-975) renders the real movementOne/movementTwo DOM inside .sk-wrap, so the denominator card sits there at its real geometry as the box the numeral will land in, ink taken out and aria-hidden. (2) The error copy quoted, 'Nothing below is shown, because a part of this screen would be guessing', is about the reading below that card; the provenance footer sits outside that scope and states what the harness is bound to, not what Tasks returned. Severity is overstated on top of that: misleading requires the product to assert something untrue, and this asserts something true about the artifact - refinement at most, and the awkwardness is a definite article in a lab-only strip that does not ship to Orla. The proposed fix is also the wrong move and would make the work worse. DENOM_STATES suppression makes the provenance line state-dependent, so in empty, loading and error the footer would claim only three figures are bound to src/lib/project-truth-fixture.ts. That is false - four are, and derive-fixture.mjs fails the build on drift of all four including openCount. It trades a slightly awkward reference for an actually untrue provenance claim in exactly the three states the finding says exist to say what is not known. A correct problem with a wrong fix is refuted; here the problem is not correct either.

refuted.problem: role="presentation" removes only the div's own role; its descendants keep theirs and stay in the accessibility tree. Read out of chromium's full AX tree over CDP at 1440 with the oldest mark focused: StaticText "41 days open" and StaticText "Confirm the marquee sides with the hire company" are both present with ignored:false, alongside the button's own accessible name ("Confirm the marquee sides with the hire company, open 41 days") and the strip's screen-reader sentence, which names all nine again. The tip is also position:fixed outside main and outside every landmark - the shape the r1 coverage-strip finding was about - and its second line is an <s>, whose meaning is content that is no longer accurate.
refuted.why: The mechanism is right and the consequence, which is the only part that would earn a change at this bar, is wrong twice over. Driven in chromium at 1440 on ?v=light&state=full with the oldest mark focused, Accessibility.getFullAXTree does show StaticText "41 days open" and StaticText "Confirm the marquee sides with the hire company" at ignored:false, and a role "deletion" node for the - role="presentation" on #tip:543 strips only the div's own role, exactly as the seat says. But walk the parent chain rather than the flat node list: the tip div is itself dropped, and its and are reparented onto body as its LAST two children, after the node that holds banner, main and contentinfo. The strings therefore land at the very end of the document, past the footer, not beside the mark. Focusing a mark announces the button's aria-label and nothing more; the tip is filled by fill() at :1084 as a plain innerHTML write into a non-live, unreferenced element (nothing carries aria-describedby to #tip), and no reader speaks an arbitrary DOM mutation outside a live region. So no user 'meets each job's title twice while it holds focus'. Second: the tip never holds nine jobs, it holds one. hide() and drop() at :1094-1095 only remove the .on class - measured after Escape, innerHTML is still 41 days openConfirm the marquee sides... - so what a browse-mode cursor actually finds at the document end is ONE stale title, whichever mark was shown last, and before any hover it is empty. Third, the implication is asserted, not measured: text-decoration is none at :386 and announcement of deletion semantics is an off-by-default per-reader setting, so 'marked up as struck-out content' is not established as something a reader hears. The fix's numbers are also wrong in two of three places: the is authored at :783 inside strip()'s data-tip, not at :1085 (:1084 is fill, :1085 is place), and the two rules are at :386-387, not :382-383. What survives is a stray, stale, orphaned string at the end of the tree - real, one attribute wide, and correctly classed refinement, meaning nothing is wrong. It does not move this engagement.

refuted.problem: The header stamps "READ AT 09:14, THURSDAY 16 JULY 2026" and the provenance strip at the foot of the same page stamps "READ 09:14, THURSDAY 16 JULY 2026" - the same string in the same uppercase mono voice, differing only by the word "at". Driven across all seven states and all four widths, the count of elements owning that text node is 2 every time. The file's own comment for the reading line says the instant is printed once, at the top, in the label voice; the gate's rule for it asserts `anchored >= 1`, so it can never see a second.
refuted.why: Every factual claim checks out and the fix is still wrong. Driven in chromium across all seven states at 390/768/1280/1440 (28 loads), the count of elements owning a text node containing LATELY_FIXTURE.readingLong is exactly 2 every time: lately.html:892 `Read at ${D.readingLong}` in the header .reading line and lately.html:902 `Read ${D.readingLong}` in the .coverage strip. Both compute to Geist Mono 11px, 400, uppercase, rgb(113,113,122) - the same voice, differing only by 'at'. The comment at lately.html:193-194 does say the instant is 'printed once, at the top', and interaction-check.mjs:352 does assert only `anchored >= 1`. So the observation is sound and the class is honest: refinement, nothing is wrong. What kills it is the fix. The .coverage strip carries aria-label 'What this reading was built from' and its comment at lately.html:467-470 states its job: what the instrument read to produce the marks. The instant IS a provenance fact - the 'as of' is the first thing a reader reconstructing a reading needs, ahead of which source answered. The seat's own consequence argues against its own fix: if the strip is 'where a reader goes once they have started to doubt the numbers', that is precisely where the anchor belongs, not where it should be deleted. The distance also defeats the collision claim. Measured at 1440 in full, the two stamps sit 1372px apart in a 960px viewport (header y=146, strip y=1518); in partial 1613, quiet 1631, first-run 1578, loading 1074. In four of seven states they are never on screen together, so the reader is not comparing two grammars - they are re-finding one fact a viewport and a half later, which is the footer-completeness convention Stripe's statement footers and Vercel's 'last updated' rails both keep. Only empty (594) and error (601) put both in one viewport, and those are the two states where the strip is the only evidence left on the page. The offered alternative, `Read this morning`, is actively worse and would breach the surface's own contract. readingLong is derived at derive-fixture.mjs:154-157 to a fixed absolute instant, 09:14 Thursday 16 July 2026; 'this morning' resolves against the reader's now, so the page would tell anyone opening it on any other day or after noon something untrue. That is the exact class this round just closed three times (august-inside-a-july-reading, error-state-invents-a-last-good-reading, first-run-shows-a-41-day-old-job) and it converts a checkable fact into an unverifiable one. The gate point is inert too: `anchored >= 1` is deliberately a floor, no rule anywhere asserts a maximum of 1, and the finding proposes no gate change - after its fix the count is 1 and the gate is exactly as blind as before. The only thing genuinely stale is the .reading comment's word 'once', and a comment is not the artifact.

a destination for a filtered list of open work, so the KPI row can carry an affordance instead of a role the screen cannot honour

rounds.headline: Clean on severity for the second consecutive round, and this one is frozen: nothing blocking, nothing misleading, from seven blind seats at the close. The number that decides the ledger is the other one — 67% of confirmed findings land on work built during round 1 and round 2's own remediation, up from 36%, and seven of the twenty-one are assertions written to close earlier findings that could not fail for the thing they named. The surface is near-finished; the repair process is now the largest single source of defects in it. Four of the five failures in this round's own verification pass were probes of mine measuring something other than their subject, caught by running them.

confirmed.element: interaction-check.mjs:1231 and :1250 — the `august-inside-a-july-reading` and `refusals-written-in-the-studio-vocabulary` blocks; same text at panel/round-1-batch4-assertions.js:96 and :115
confirmed.problem: Both blocks build their patterns with four source backslashes: `new RegExp("\\\\b" + m + "\\\\b(?!\\\\s+\\\\d{4})", "g")` and `new RegExp("\\\\b" + w + "\\\\b", "i")`. Four backslashes in JS source yield the two-character escape `\\`, so the compiled pattern is a LITERAL backslash followed by `b`, not a word boundary. I cut lines 1231 and 1250 out of the file byte-for-byte with sed (od -c confirms four 0x5C bytes), ran them unmodified under node, and got: `re.source` = `\\bAugust\\b(?!\\s+\\d{4})`; `.test("finished in August, before")` = false; the banned-vocabulary filter run over "the callers accrues periods provider structured recorder" = []. Page text never contains a backslash, so `found` and `hits` are permanently empty. That is eight assertions — `no month is named without its year` and `the refusals speak the reader's language`, each across full/partial/quiet/first-run — that cannot fail for any content whatsoever. I then re-ran the SAME two checks with single escapes against the live surface in chromium at 1440 in all four states: bareMonths [], banned hits [], the only year-bearing strings being "June 2027" and (first-run) "August 2026". So the surface's behaviour is correct and only the checks are dead. The mechanism is lessons.md L-12 creeping back in its mirror form — over-escaped rather than under-escaped — through the one tool built to stop it: panel/append-assertions.mjs's own header comment says a regex written through a shell "silently made the checks vacuous. lessons.md L-12", and the block it spliced carries the same defect.
confirmed.consequence: The engagement's record reads 461 assertions, all green. Eight of them are theatre. Two confirmed round-1 findings are carried as closed on the strength of checks that would sail through a total regression — put the month back without its year, or write the refusals in studio vocabulary again, and the gate still prints pass. Under L-05 ("a finding is closed only when something asserts it") those two are not closed, and the ledger this engagement ends on is overstating its own coverage by eight.
confirmed.fix: Two edits per file, with a file-editing tool, never through a heredoc (this environment's shell halves backslashes in a quoted heredoc — I confirmed it while reproducing this). (1) interaction-check.mjs:1250 and panel/round-1-batch4-assertions.js:115: `const hits = banned.filter((w) => new RegExp("\\b" + w + "\\b", "i").test(text));` — two source backslashes each; verified green in all four states. (2) interaction-check.mjs:1231 and panel/round-1-batch4-assertions.js:96 need two backslashes AND a guard against the short-form date labels, or they go red on "4 May": `const re = new RegExp("(?<!\\d\\s)\\b" + m + "\\b(?!\\s+\\d{4})", "g");` — a month immediately preceded by a day-of-month number is a date, not a bare month. Driven at 1440 in all four states this returns [] on the live surface, and appending "finished in August, before the week is out" to the page text makes it return ["August"] in every state, so it still catches the exact regression it was written for. Add a third `ok()` beside them asserting the instrument itself is alive — e.g. that the same regex applied to a fixed literal probe string returns the expected hit — so this class cannot recur silently in either direction. Then re-run the full gate and re-state its assertion count.
confirmed.assertion: Add a self-test immediately above the two blocks, so the gate proves its own patterns before it trusts them: `ok("the gate's own word-boundary patterns compile as word boundaries", new RegExp("\\b" + "August" + "\\b(?!\\s+\\d{4})").test("finished in August, before") === true && new RegExp("\\bAugust\\b(?!\\s+\\d{4})").test("in August 2026") === false && new RegExp("\\b" + "callers" + "\\b", "i").test("the callers did not answer") === true);`. Then prove the two repaired blocks can fail: with `F.comparisonArrives` temporarily set to "10 August", `no month is named without its year · first-run` must FAIL, and must pass again at "10 August 2026"; with the word "provider" injected into a LIMITS body, `the refusals speak the reader's language · full` must FAIL.
confirmed.verdict: problem affirmed, seat's fix replaced — The defect is real and I reproduced it exactly; the finding is refuted on its fix and on one of its own load-bearing measurements. VERIFIED TRUE: od -c on interaction-check.mjs:1231 and :1250 shows four 0x5C bytes in each escape (and grep for four-backslash sequences finds exactly those two lines in the whole gate, plus the same two lines at panel/round-1-batch4-assertions.js:96 and :115). Run under node with the bytes preserved by a file-editing tool, `re.source` is `\\bAugust\\b(?!\\s+\\d{4})` — a literal backslash then b — `.test("finished in August, before")` is false, and the banned-vocabulary filter over "the callers accrues periods provider structured recorder" returns []. main innerText contains no backslash in any of the four states (checked), so `found` and `hits` are structurally empty and eight assertions (`no month is named without its year` and `the refusals speak the reader's language`, each x full/partial/quiet/first-run) cannot fail. That much stands, and it is the class the round notes say is worth the most. VERIFIED FALSE: the finding's claim that it re-ran the same two checks with single escapes against the live surface and got 'bareMonths []' in all four states. Driven in chromium at 1440, reducedMotion, ?v=light&state=<state>, with `new RegExp("\\b" + m + "\\b(?!\\s+\\d{4})", "g")` — i.e. the finding's own proposed line 1231 verbatim — bareMonths is ["May"] in full, partial AND quiet. The hit is the chart's screen-reader description: "twelve weeks of finished work, week commencing 27 Apr to 13 Jul: 27 Apr, 5; 4 May, 3; 11 May, 6; 18 May, 4; 25 May, 7; 1 Jun, 5; ...". May is the one month whose abbreviation equals its full name, so the month list matches the short-form date labels; Apr/Jun/Jul do not collide and first-run has no such strip, which is why first-run alone comes back []. So the proposed fix does not restore a green gate — it turns three of the eight assertions red on a correct, frozen surface, in the closing round, on a false positive (a day-and-month inside an explicitly bounded, explicitly dated range is not the bare month in prose that august-inside-a-july-reading was about). A fix that makes the measured baseline red is worse than the vacuity it replaces, and it fails its own stated standard of proof: the seat reports a measurement it evidently did not get. The banned-vocabulary half of the fix (line 1250 / :115) is correct as written — with two backslashes, hits is [] in all four states. Severity is not overstated: defect is right. Nothing on the product surface is wrong — driven, no month is named without its year in prose, no studio vocabulary survives, the only year-bearing strings are "June 2027" and (first-run) "August 2026" — so this is a dead instrument, not a product that asserts something untrue. L-05 does bite on the record: those two round-1 closures currently rest on checks that cannot fail, and the 461-green count is overstating coverage by eight until the corrected lines land.

confirmed.verdict: problem affirmed, seat's fix replaced — The vacuity is real and I proved it, but the finding is wrong about its own counterfactual and its fix would turn the gate red on the correct surface, so it is refuted with the corrected fix carried. WHAT CHECKS OUT. interaction-check.mjs:534 is `Number(early.record) < Number(late.record) || early.lastBar < late.lastBar`, and the right-hand disjunct is a term of line 532's own test that the entrance runs. Driven in chromium at 1440x960, ?state=full&v=light&motion=play, with the gate's exact sampling (200ms, then +2000ms): early={hero:28,lastBar:0,record:'0'}, late={hero:31,lastBar:168,record:'1'}. I re-ran the block with `.record` forced to `animation:none;opacity:1;clip-path:none` injected at DOMContentLoaded - the previous best painted from the first frame, before a single column, the exact inversion the assertion names - and line 534 still passed, because early.lastBar 0 < late.lastBar 168 carries it alone. Line 534 is also the only assertion in the file that touches the record's ordering (the other `.record` hits are 524/530 sampling, 638 label overlap, 660-668 record-tag-never-paints, 1063-1067 degraded state, 1436 skeleton visibility). So the headline stands: the assertion cannot fail for its own claim. WHY IT IS REFUTED ANYWAY. (1) The finding's stated counterfactual is false when driven. It claims that removing the 1.1s animation-delay would make the left disjunct go false. It does not: with `.record{animation-delay:0s}` the 0.6s draw is still mid-flight at the 200ms sample, so early.record=0.877 < late.record=1 and the LEFT disjunct is true too. The only counterfactual that actually isolates the vacuity is the no-animation one above, which the finding does not name. (2) The proposed fix is wrong against the real source and would fail the shipped, compliant surface. Its arithmetic is right - `.bar` is `grow 0.5s` at `calc(var(--i)*40ms + 340ms)` (lately.html:255-256), so the twelfth column runs 780-1280ms - but its threshold is not. `.record` is `draw 0.6s` at `animation-delay:1.1s` (lately.html:303) over `@keyframes draw{from{opacity:0}to{opacity:1}}` (line 518), so at 1280ms the record is already ~30% through its own fade: measured 0.849 at t=1294ms, and a poll loop that waits for the twelfth column's height to stop changing actually lands at ~1399ms where opacity reads 0.966. The fix requires that frame to be under 0.5. It would go red on a surface whose choreography is exactly right, which is a worse fault in a gate than the vacuous assertion it replaces. (3) The fix's premise is also slightly off: the record does not begin after the columns finish - it starts at 1100ms while the twelfth column is still growing to 1280ms - so any assertion phrased as 'record starts after the last column ends' fails on the master too. What is true, and is what the choreography actually claims, is that no part of the old ceiling is visible while the columns are being drawn (opacity is exactly 0 until 1100ms, with the twelfth column already at 162.6/168px by 1043ms) and it completes after they have all settled. The seat's `defect` is the right class for the underlying vacuity - nothing on screen is wrong, the choreography measures correct, and what is missing is the guard - so I do not correct it upward; but the finding as filed does not earn a change because acting on it as written breaks the gate.

confirmed.element: .ghost-say .t-head, .center .t-body, .kpi > .t-small, .ages h3.t-head, .hero-note (first-run)
confirmed.problem: `text-wrap` computes to `wrap` on every element on the surface — no `balance`, no `pretty`, no non-breaking bindings anywhere. Driven across all seven states, four widths and both grounds, five distinct blocks end on a single word: the ghost plot's centred 20px caption breaks "Open work over time — the chart that would go / here", four characters centred under a 45-character line, at 768, 900, 1280 and 1440; the quiet state's centred body ends on "else." alone, 31px of a 436px measure; the empty state's centred body ends on "things." alone; the fifth KPI label ends on "else" alone at 1280 and 1440 while its four neighbours sit on one line, and at 390 the first card ends on "fortnight" alone; and the first-run note breaks the comparison date itself — "Yours arrive on 10 August / 2026." — at every one of the four declared widths. Two of the five are centred, which is where a one-word last line is most conspicuous, and both sit inside protected objects.
confirmed.consequence: The owner is never misled, but the surface stops looking typeset. A four-letter word alone and centred in the middle of the drawn-but-empty plot is the first thing the eye lands on in that figure, and it undercuts the argument that object exists to make. Splitting "10 August" from "2026" is worse than a plain widow: the one date a first-run owner is being told to wait for arrives in two pieces on two lines.
confirmed.fix: Add to the stylesheet: `.ghost-say .t-head, .center .t-sect, .center .t-body, .kpi > .t-small, .ages .band-head .t-head { text-wrap: balance; }` and `.limit .t-small, .hero-note, .note .t-body { text-wrap: pretty; }`. Separately, stop the comparison date breaking at render time rather than in the generated fixture: in the `first-run` view in lately.html, replace `${esc(D.comparisonArrives)}` with `${esc(D.comparisonArrives).replace(/ /g, "\u00a0")}`.
confirmed.assertion: For every state at 390, 768, 900, 1280 and 1440, every element matching `.ghost-say .t-head`, `.center .t-body`, `.kpi > .t-small`, `.ages .band-head .t-head` or `.hero-note` whose text runs to more than one line has a last line carrying either two or more words or at least 30% of the width of its own longest line; and in `first-run` the string "10 August 2026" occupies exactly one line box.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed. Driven in chromium across all seven states, at 390/768/1280/1440, on both grounds, measuring every line box with word-level Ranges. `text-wrap` computes to `wrap`/`auto` on every element named, and the count of one-word last lines is 42 on light and 42 on dark - identical, so this is not a ground artefact. Every specific claim reproduces: the ghost caption breaks "Open work over time - the chart that would go" [437px] / "here" [41px] at 768, 1280 and 1440 (clean at 390, where the caption box is 340px); quiet's centred body ends "else." at 31px under a 436px line at 768/1280/1440; empty's ends "things." at 46px; `.kpi > .t-small`#4 breaks "are waiting on something" / "else" [25px] at 1280 and 1440 while cards 0-3 all sit on one line (verified nlines=1 for each), and at 390 the fortnight card ends on "fortnight" [52px]; the first-run note ends on "2026." [35px] at all four widths. Two further instances the write-up did not enumerate: `.ages .band-head .t-head` ends on "sitting" [59px] at 390 in every state that draws it. Both gates were read first - neither `interaction-check.mjs` (461 assertions) nor `audit.mjs` contains any string matching text-wrap, so this restates nothing either gate proves, and `lessons.md` has no widow/orphan class, so nothing is creeping back. The fix is right against the real source. All eight selectors resolve to real elements (`.ghost-say .t-head` lately.html:447, `.center .t-body` :457, `.kpi > .t-small` :347, `.hero-note` :240, `.limit` :434, `.note .t-body` :451, `.ages` band-head h3.t-head :841); the Element line's `.ages h3.t-head` and the fix's `.ages .band-head .t-head` are the same node. `${esc(D.comparisonArrives)}` occurs exactly once in a view (:997, first-run), so the replace lands where claimed, after `esc()` (no double-escape) and at render time, leaving `fixture.js` and `derive-fixture.mjs` untouched - which is why it does not disturb the build's sentence-vs-marks check. I applied the fix verbatim to a copy of the lab and re-measured: all 42 one-word last lines go to zero on both grounds, and box widths and line counts are byte-identical to baseline across all 28 state x width combinations - the change is purely where the break falls, not how tall anything is. `interaction-check.mjs` returns 461 assertions, 0 failing, with output that diffs identical to baseline; `audit.mjs` returns all-zero totals, output identical to baseline. The severity class is correct and not overstated: nothing is asserted untrue and nothing is unreadable, so refinement, not defect - though the date break is the one instance that edges toward defect, since splitting "10 August" from "2026" is a typesetting error rather than a preference. It earns a change at this bar because it is one layout-neutral declaration block against the finish Linear, Stripe and Vercel ship as standard, and because two of the five sit centred inside protected objects - a 41px orphan under the drawn-but-empty plot is the first thing the eye lands on in the object whose whole argument is that it looks like the chart it would be.
confirmed.breaks: The two halves must land together or the fix regresses the thing it was written for. `text-wrap: pretty` on `.hero-note` WITHOUT the non-breaking date does not fix the first-run note - it relocates the break inside the date, to "Yours arrive on 10" / "August 2026.", which is worse than the widow it replaced. Measured at all four widths. With both halves the note reads "...Yours arrive on" / "10 August 2026." and stays at 3 lines. Re-measure after it lands: (1) line counts, since `pretty` can add a line by rebalancing the tail - it does not here (verified identical across 7 states x 4 widths x 2 grounds), but any later copy change can move it, and `.kpi > .t-small` carries `flex: 1 1 auto` so an added line would grow the KPI row; (2) the 259px `.hero-note` measure, since the date becomes one unbreakable 97px token - safe at 390 today and safe for any longer month, but it is now an overflow surface where it was not before; (3) `.ages .band-head .t-head` is a flex item in a wrapping row, where `balance` can interact with shrink-to-fit sizing - its box measured 308px at 390 and 341px at 1440 both before and after, unchanged. Two cheap costs worth accepting knowingly: copying the date out of the page yields NBSPs rather than spaces, and browser find-in-page for "10 August 2026" is not guaranteed to match. Where `balance`/`pretty` are unsupported the declaration degrades to `wrap`, i.e. exactly today's rendering - no fallback needed. Two slips in the write-up, neither load-bearing: the ghost caption's first line is 44 characters, not 45, and "at 768, 900, 1280 and 1440" mixes a frame height into a list of widths - the declared widths are 390/768/1280/1440 and the caption orphan is present at the upper three and absent at 390.

Do not reach for white-space: nowrap on .coverage span instead - at 390 the stamp is 7.2px wider than its 342px container, so nowrap converts a wrap into an overflow. While the file is open, close the hole the finding actually found by making the gate able to fail: after the existing coverage assertions, assert at 390 that no .coverage span's last line box is narrower than two glyphs - e.g. for each span take Array.from(document.createRange() over its contents .getClientRects()), group by rounded top, and require the last group's total width > 16px. confirmed.verdict: Every measurement in this finding checks out when driven, and the fix delivers exactly what it claims. The stamp's unwrapped width is 349.2px (identical at 414, 768, 1280 and 1440, where it sets on one line). At 390 the .coverage content box is exactly 342px, so the stamp overflows by 7.2px and wraps to two lines: line one runs 24 -> 358 and ends after 'THE', and line two is a single client rect 7.6px wide at x=24. 7.6px is exactly one glyph of 11px Geist Mono at 0.99px tracking (the 33-character READ stamp measures 250.5px, 7.59px/char), so the second line is the bare digit 9 and nothing else. The element screenshot of .coverage at 390 confirms it: 'BOUND WORKSPACE, OWNER, READING DATE AND THE' then '9' alone. It reproduces in full, partial, quiet, first-run, empty, loading and error at 390, and in the dark twin; it clears at 414 and above, so 390 and 360 are the exposed widths (at 360 the widow is 'THE 9', at 320 'AND THE 9' plus the Lab stamp also wraps). The gate observation at interaction-check.mjs:259-267 is also right and is the more valuable half: the comment claims both halves are 'short enough for the stamp voice it is set in' and cites the 134-character string that ran too long, but the assertion beneath it is only /lab-authored/ && /Bound/ && /reading date/ on textContent - three presence tests. confirmed.element: lately.html — `hide()` in the tooltip block (~L1168) and the `pointerleave` listener on every `[data-tip]`
confirmed.problem: `hide()` guards only the touch pin: `if (pinned && !force) return; tip.classList.remove("on"); showing = null;`. It does not guard focus. Driven in chromium at 1440, ?state=full&v=light: Tab to `.dot` nth(2) — the ring paints (`:focus-visible` true) and the tip names "Send the midweek rate to the June 2027 couple, 5 days open". Move the real pointer onto that same mark (tip still on, correct), then 400px away. `pointerleave` fires, `hide()` clears the tip and nulls `showing`. Measured immediately after: tip `on` = false, `document.activeElement` still the same dot, still matching `:focus-visible`. It does not come back — `onMove` returns on `!showing`, so a subsequent 40px scroll leaves it off (measured). Only Tab-away-and-Tab-back recovers it. The same happens if the pointer merely crosses a DIFFERENT mark and leaves: I focused dot nth(1), hovered dot nth(8) (the tip correctly retargeted to "41 days open / Confirm the marquee sides…", overwriting the focused mark's label), then moved away — tip off, dot nth(1) still ringed and now unnamed.
confirmed.consequence: This is exactly the state the round-2 note says the scroll path was written to prevent: "dropping a focused mark's label leaves a visibly focused mark with no name anywhere on the screen." The job title lives in no other pixel on this surface. confirmed.assertion: For each of light and dark at 1440, ?state=full: focus `.dot` nth(2) by keyboard, assert `#tip` has class `on` and `#tip.textContent` contains the focused dot's `aria-label` title. Then move the real pointer onto that dot's centre and then to 400px away; after 250ms assert `#tip` STILL has class `on` and still names the focused dot. Repeat with the pointer travelling over `.dot` nth(8) before leaving — the tip must return to naming nth(2), not stay on nth(8) and not go off. Then press Escape and assert it does go off, so the explicit dismissal is not broken.
confirmed.verdict: problem affirmed, seat's fix replaced — Every measurement in the finding reproduces exactly, and the fix it proposes creates a worse defect than the one it closes. THE PROBLEM IS REAL. Driven in chromium at 1440, ?v=light&state=full, 9 marks: focus .dot nth(2) -> tip on, text '5 days open / Send the midweek rate to the June 2027 couple', activeElement the dot, :focus-visible true. Pointer onto the same mark -> still on, correct. Pointer 400px away -> tip on=false, activeElement STILL that dot, :focus-visible STILL true. A subsequent 40px window scroll does not bring it back (onMove returns on !showing); only Tab-away-and-Tab-back recovers it. The cross-mark case reproduces too: focus nth(1) ('Confirm the Harbour wall cordon with the harbourmaster'), hover nth(8) -> tip retargets to '41 days open / Confirm the marquee sides with the hire company' while nth(1) stays ringed, then pointer away -> tip off, nth(1) ringed, :focus-visible true, unnamed. The keyboard-only baseline is the control and it is clean: focus + 40px scroll leaves the tip on. So hide() at ~L1168 does contradict the comment eight lines below it ('a focus-raised tip is hidden and restored when its mark comes back; only a touch pin is retired, because dropping a focused mark's label leaves a visibly focused mark with no name anywhere on the screen'), and nothing in interaction-check.mjs L449-497 mixes a pointer with a held focus, so this is genuinely past what the gate sees. THE FIX IS WRONG. It guards on `held.dataset.tip` alone, and its stated justification -- 'by then document.activeElement is no longer a mark' -- is true only for blur. It is false for a mouse click. Measured: hover .dot nth(2) in view, mouse down, mouse up -> document.activeElement IS the dot, dataset.tip IS set, and :focus-visible is FALSE (no ring paints; the click handler preventDefaults, so the mark is deliberately clickable-and-inert). Move the pointer 300px away and today the tip correctly goes off. Under the proposed hide(), that same pointerleave would hit `held.dataset.tip` -> show(held) and the tooltip would stick to a mark that carries no ring, with no hover and no visible focus to explain it. onMove would then keep it alive across scroll (`document.activeElement === showing`), and leaving any OTHER mark would snap the tip back to the clicked one. The only exits are Escape or a click elsewhere. That is an undismissable tooltip for the ordinary mouse user -- a larger and far more reachable population than the focus-plus-mouse case being fixed -- so the fix trades a narrow defect for a broader one. Confirmed also that `document.activeElement` during blur is BODY in this build, so the fix's blur reasoning is the one part that holds. Severity of the underlying problem is correctly classed defect, not misleading: nothing untrue is asserted, the mark keeps its aria-label ('Send the midweek rate to the June 2027 couple, open 5 days') so a screen reader is unaffected, the ring persists, and Tab-away/back recovers. Correct problem, wrong fix -- refuted, corrected fix below.
confirmed.breaks: The sharpened fix, not the seat's. Re-measure: (a) interaction-check.mjs L449-455 (fine-pointer hover names the mark; tip stays inside the window) -- the restored tip is re-place()d against the FOCUSED mark, not the one the pointer left, so its position assertion must be re-run with focus held; (b) L489-497, keyboard reaches every mark and Escape dismisses -- Escape still works on the keystroke, but note the residual: after Escape the mark stays focused and :focus-visible, so the next pointerleave anywhere on the strip will resurrect the tip. If that is unacceptable, add an `escaped` flag set in drop() and cleared in the focus handler, and assert it; (c) L1194-1217 stale-tip-strands-on-scroll at 390 with touch -- unaffected by construction (pointerleave returns early for touch and the `!pinned` guard holds), but re-run it, since a hybrid fine+coarse device is the one place the two paths meet; (d) the .tip is pointer-events:none, so a restored tip cannot intercept the pointer or re-trigger enter/leave -- verified, but re-check if the tip ever gains pointer-events. confirmed.element: lately.html:401 — .dot:hover, .dot:focus-visible { --disc: var(--ink); } — against the touch pin in the pointerdown handler at lately.html:1187
confirmed.problem: Under a coarse pointer the browser latches :hover onto the last element touched and never releases it. Driven at 390x844 with hasTouch and isMobile, using a real touchscreen.tap on the first mark: at rest the dot computes --disc #71717a; after one tap el.matches(':hover') is true and --disc is #111111 with the ::before ring at rgb(17, 17, 17); after the second tap that dismisses the tip (tip.classList.contains('on') === false) the mark is still #111111; after scrolling the document 300px it is still #111111. The mark is left carrying the surface's strongest ink with no state behind it — not pinned, not focused, not past the fortnight.
confirmed.consequence: The strip's entire reading is carried by fill and ink density: a hollow ring inside the fortnight, a solid indigo mark past it. A residue of an interaction the reader already dismissed makes one arbitrary young mark the most emphatic mark in the strip, and it stays that way for the rest of the session. 390 is the width where the tooltip is the only place a job's title lives, so it is the width where a reader taps marks most — every tap leaves another false emphasis behind. The lock's rule is that status is ink density and fill; this puts ink density on a mark that has no status.

The same latch is on the tab strip and it is the more consequential one: .tab:hover { color: var(--ink); } at lately.html:196, on anchors that are href="#" and navigate nowhere. Measured at 390 with touch: at rest the two inactive tabs are rgb(113,113,122)/400 and Lately is rgb(17,17,17)/600; after one tap on 'Today's Signal' it is rgb(17,17,17)/400 and stays there through a 600px scroll. Two tabs then read at full ink and only weight 600 and the 2px ::after underline still separate the current one, so the tap degrades the surface's navigation signal, not just a chart mark. Move that rule into the same gate: replace .tab:hover { color: var(--ink); } with @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) { .tab:hover { color: var(--ink); } }, keeping it before .tab[aria-current="page"] so the current tab's ink and weight are untouched. confirmed.element: the three `.tab` anchors in `shell()` — `<a class="tab t-body" href="#">`, including the one carrying `aria-current="page"`
confirmed.problem: All three tabs are anchors to a bare `#`. Driven in chromium at 1440, ?state=full&v=light: with the document scrolled to y=684, focusing "Today's Signal" and pressing Enter moves the URL to `…&v=light#`, sets `scrollY` to 0 and takes `history.length` from 2 to 3, while `aria-current` stays on "Lately" and not one pixel of the surface changes. Separately, measuring rest/hover/press from what paints: the two sibling tabs go ink-3 → ink on hover and then do not move on press; the current tab measures `rgb(17,17,17)` at rest, on hover and under a held pointer — it is the only focusable control on this surface with no hover state and no press state at all. This is the same bare-`#` href round 2 removed from the KPI cards ("the cards were link roles whose href appended a bare `#`"); the fix landed on one object and not on the other.
confirmed.consequence: A reader who presses the sibling tabs to find out why nothing happened gets no press feedback that the click even landed, and silently spends one Back press per attempt. confirmed.fix: Do not guard all three tabs. The only durable one-liner is the self-link on the tab that is already current, which has nowhere to go in the prototype or in the shipped app: after the [data-tip] listener loop in lately.html (~line 1212) add `const cur = root.querySelector('.tab[aria-current=\"page\"]'); if (cur) cur.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.preventDefault());`. That removes the one stray history entry and the snap without touching the two tabs that will carry real routes — and it survives the port, because a current tab must not re-navigate to itself. The two siblings should keep an href and get their real routes on the port packet; guarding them now trades a stray fragment for a tab that visibly does nothing, which is the worse of the two. Leave the press states alone: a selected tab that does not react to a press is correct, not missing.

confirmed.element: .limit .t-small (the three refusal bodies) and .note .t-body, between 561px and 900px
confirmed.problem: `.limit .t-small` carries no max-width at all, and `.limits` collapses to one column at `max-width: 900px`. Driven in chromium and measured by word ranges, the third refusal body sets 121 characters on a line at 900px, 118 at 899, 103 at 793 and 792, and 97 at the declared 768 viewport that has a committed frame. confirmed.consequence: In the movement the brief protects as the product's signature, the owner reads three unbroken 120-character lines of 13px type on a tablet. At that measure the return sweep loses the line — the eye cannot reliably find the start of the next one — and the refusals stop reading as designed statements and start reading as unstyled paragraph text. It is the one movement whose whole job is to be believed, and it is set worst at the width a venue owner is most likely to hold.
confirmed.fix: Keep the ceiling, drop the other two rules, and set the number from what paints rather than from ch -- which is the finding's own argument, applied to its own fix. Driven, 330px yields 49/58 - 53/54 - 55/54 across the band and is inert at 1440 (column content box 318.7px) and at 390 (310px), so it bites only where the grid has collapsed and it lands the band on the same 49-55 measure the three-column layout already delivers -- which is what the seat promised and what its own 42ch does not deliver: 42ch computes to 361.998px and yields up to 64 characters on line one, about 16% wider than the measure it claims to match. (2) DROP `.limit .t-head { max-width: 40ch }` entirely. 40ch at 20px computes to 546.4px; the three heads are 16-20 characters and render at 171/193/180px, so this rule can never bite at any width from 390 to 1440. It is inert CSS shipped into a stylesheet this lab has already had a finding filed against for dead rules. (3) LEAVE `.note .t-body { max-width: 62ch }` out of this change, or take it as its own decision with its own frames. Its 91-character line is real but it is not a tablet-band defect -- it is identical at 1440 and 1280 -- so folding it in here smuggles a change to the partial state at the reference width in under a band-scoped rationale. And 46ch computes to 457.47px and yields 66/69, not the 48-54 the finding names as the design's intent; if it is taken at all the honest number is ~300px (the note is a flex row, so a narrower body also changes how much of the panel the paragraph fills, which is a composition call, not a measure call).
