refuted.problem: The hero card keeps the full-state two-column grid — minmax(220px,300px) 1fr — while its second column holds a plot narrowed to 57px. Measured in chromium at 1440: card 1084x268.9; figure column 231->531; chart column 579->1265 with .cols, .baseline and the ruler all clamped to 579->636. From the right edge of the only painted mark to the card's inner edge is 629px of unclaimed white, 58% of the card, with nothing drawn in it — not even the axis, because .plot.solo .baseline is narrowed to 57px too, so the floor stops as a 57px stub. At 1280 the same 629px. At 900 and below the hero stacks and the card becomes 483.8px tall with a 698px chart row holding 57px of mark and a 641px void; at 390, 251px of void in a 467.8px-tall card. The column pitch and the narrow ruler are both argued in source and both closed in earlier rounds — this finding does not touch either. The card's width is the part nothing argues.
refuted.why: The observation measures out; the fix is broken at three of the five widths it claims to cover, and it breaks the one composition the source explicitly protects. MEASURED (chromium, ?v=light&state=first-run&motion=settled). At 1440 the card is 1084x268.9 at 206->1290, .hero resolves to 300px 686px with a 48px gap, .hero-fig 231->531, .chart 579->1265, and .cols/.baseline/.plot.solo~.xaxis all clamped to 579->636. So the 629px figure is real, but it is the distance from the baseline's right edge to the chart's right edge, not 'from the right edge of the only painted mark': the rightmost painted thing is the .bar-val label '12 so far', 68.3px wide, running to 647.3, which leaves 618.7px to the card's inner edge (1266) - 57% of the card, not 58%. That 68.3 matters, because it is the number the fix gets wrong. THE FIX, DRIVEN. Rule 1, `[data-state="first-run"] .hero { grid-template-columns: minmax(220px,300px) auto; }`, has specificity (0,2,0) and the phone rule at lately.html:554, `.hero { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }` inside `@media (max-width:900px)`, has (0,1,0). A media query does not add specificity, so the stacked hero never comes back. Injected and measured, the computed grid at 900 is `300px 86px`, at 768 `300px 86px`, at 560 `300px 102px`, at 390 `252px 32px` - two columns at every width. The finding's claim that 'at 900 and below the existing stacked grid takes over' is false, and the phone composition argued at lately.html:549-553 ('Not a reduction: the hero stacks so the numeral keeps its scale') is deleted by rule 1 alone. At 390 it is not merely different, it is broken: .cols keeps its fixed 57px inside a 32px track and the card reports scrollWidth-clientWidth = 20; captured, the hatched column, the '12 SO FAR' label and the '13 JUL' tick are all sliced by the card's right border. Nothing catches it downstream - .scroll is `overflow-x: clip`, so document overflow still reads 0 and the gate's overflow probes stay green while the only mark on the state hangs off the card. Rule 2's arithmetic is wrong too. '24+300+48+57+24 = 453 in a 460 box' sizes the chart track to the 57px column, but every mark in .plot.solo is absolutely positioned, so the track's content width comes from the 57px .xaxis and `auto` then stretches under normal justify-content: measured at 1440 the track is 62px, the card is exactly 460, and the .bar-val label runs to 647.3 against an inner edge of 642 - the label sits inside the right padding with 18.7px of gutter, not 24. The 460 box does not contain the content it was sized for. On severity: even with a working fix this is a refinement, not a defect. Nothing is wrong, unreadable or untrue here - the sparseness is the honest consequence of two protected decisions (no ghost slots, no scale from one datum), the mark carries its own value and its own date within 68px of itself after the r2 fix, and a wide card with air on its right is a density judgment a studio could take either way. On a frozen closing round that is not worth moving a pixel with a rule that costs the phone.

refuted.problem: Driven at ?state=partial: the band head reads "All five counted out of 9" and the lead card speaks "Every card in this row is counted out of these 9 open jobs." Forty pixels below, the due-date card prints an em dash, the words "Not available", and no meter. Measured from the DOM: 5 cards, 3 carrying a meter, 1 unavailable. Four cards are counted out of nine; the header says five, twice — once in ink and once in the accessibility tree. This is the self-contradicting-counts class from the paid defect library ("a header saying 5 of 32 done above a tray labelled 9"), and it is the one place on the surface where the honest-degradation contract is not honoured: everywhere else the missing source resolves to unavailable, here the summary above it quietly counts it.
refuted.why: The mechanism is real and the consequence built on it is not, and the fix is wrong three ways. Driven in chromium at 1440/1280/768/390, light and dark, reducedMotion, at ?state=partial and ?state=full. Confirmed: the band head prints the typed literal 'All five counted out of 9' (lately.html:861, hardcoded, state-blind), the row holds 5 .kpi (1 .lead + 4 status), 1 carries .na and no meter, 3 carry meters, and .kpi.lead .sr speaks the unconditional 'Every card in this row is counted out of these 9 open jobs.' (lately.html:756). So the word 'five' is loose by one in exactly one state. Everything the finding derives from that is wrong. (1) The consequence assumes the cards are parts of a whole - 'is the missing due-date count included in the nine or not?' There is nothing to include. D.open is F.bound.openCount, a Tasks-derived bound figure the build gates; the four status cards are overlapping subsets of it, not addends. In full the row reads 3, 2, 1, 0 against 9 - the numbers already do not sum, and no reader is summing them. Whether Timeline answered cannot move the nine, so the question the owner is said to be stuck on has no bearing on any figure on the screen and the shared-denominator claim is untouched: every card that has a reading is still read against the same 9. (2) 'they must decide which to believe' does not survive the frame. Screenshotted at 1440, the stamp is tracked uppercase mono, dim, flush right in the band head - a scale legend, not a headline - and the card 27px under it prints an em-dash rule where a numeral goes, no meter, and the words NOT AVAILABLE, with a note directly beneath the row reading 'Timeline did not answer this reading, so nothing here knows a due date. The card keeps its place and says so; it does not fall back to zero.' The fact is stated three times in ink before any reader reaches an ambiguity. The honest-degradation contract is 'a reader can never mistake we-don't-know for it's-zero'; nothing here offers a zero or any number to mistake. (3) The one measurement offered is wrong at every width driven: the label's bottom sits 27px above the unavailable card at 1440 and 1280, and 166px/169px at 390/768 where the row stacks. 'Forty pixels below' matches no width. Severity is overstated on top of that. defect requires something visibly wrong; what is visible is a legend that says five where four carry readings, corrected in ink twice within one card-height. That is refinement, and an overstated class is itself a reason to refute. The fix is worse than the looseness. (a) It puts three numerals into the row's only denominator declaration - 'Four of five counted out of 9' - so the stamp whose whole job is to name the one shared base now invites the part-of-whole arithmetic that does not exist, and demotes a protected object to a caveat about card availability. (b) The sr rewrite re-opens a closed round-2 finding. kpi-cards-announce-their-fact-twice moved the row's sentence onto the group's own name so each card is announced once; the unavailability already exists in the tree exactly once, on the NA card's aria-label 'Jobs past the day they were due: not available, because Timeline did not answer'. Appending '; the due-date card was not read.' to the lead card's sr announces it a second time in the tree and a fourth time on the surface. (c) Its arithmetic never matches its own output: `const counted = 4 - (partial ? 1 : 0)` counts status cards, so counted is 3 in partial and 4 in full, then it prints 'Four of five' when counted is 3 and 'All five' when counted is 4 - the variable equals the printed number in neither branch. And it does not do the thing it advertises: 'derive the label from the row rather than typing it' is delivered as two more typed strings keyed off the same `partial` boolean that already drives `unavailable`. Nothing is read from the row.

refuted.problem: Round 2 established the rule on this surface: a state that says it is still reading may not publish the reading, and every magnitude in the skeleton was neutralised in place to honour it. The coverage footer was not. Driven at ?state=loading&motion=settled, its six entries read, in one row, in one grammar: "Tasks reading · Timeline reading · Notes reading · Read 09:14, Thursday 16 July 2026 · Lab counts and ages are lab-authored · Bound workspace, owner, reading date and the 9". Three entries say the read is in progress and the fourth, immediately beside them and in the same voice, says when it completed. The reading line at the top of the page prints the same stamp a second time ("Read at 09:14, Thursday 16 July 2026"), at full ink, above a page that has been emptied of every other fact. Two text nodes carry `readingLong` in this state; both are magnitudes the state does not hold.
refuted.why: The strings are quoted correctly and the reading of them is wrong, and the fix would reintroduce the exact jump round 2 removed. WHAT DRIVES TRUE. At ?v=light&state=loading&motion=settled, 1440x960, chromium: .coverage reads TASKS READING | TIMELINE READING | NOTES READING | READ 09:14, THURSDAY 16 JULY 2026 | LAB COUNTS AND AGES ARE LAB-AUTHORED | BOUND WORKSPACE, OWNER, READING DATE AND THE 9, and exactly two elements own a text node containing readingLong (.reading p at lately.html:944, the .coverage span at :954). That much is right. WHAT KILLS IT. (1) The stamp is not a completion receipt, and the error state proves it. Driven at ?state=error the same two stamps print at the same coordinates (reading line y=122.14, coverage y=583.88) beside TASKS DID NOT ANSWER | TIMELINE NOT READ | NOTES NOT READ. Three sources say the read failed and the fourth, in the same row and the same voice, prints 09:14, Thursday 16 July 2026 - the finding's structural complaint, verbatim, in a state where the read demonstrably did not happen. That is not an oversight: interaction-check.mjs:353-362 runs the anchored loop over full, partial, quiet, first-run AND error and asserts the instant is stated in each, while the separate error check at :1004-1013 counts stamps inside main only and passes at 0. The surface deliberately keeps the anchor when the read fails and deliberately keeps it out of the reading. So READ is not 'when it completed'; it is the instant everything relative on the screen resolves against, which is what lately.html:204-205 says it is. In loading that anchor is still load-bearing: TWELVE WEEKS sits immediately to its right in the same row, and twelve weeks is meaningless without an end. (2) Applied evenly the finding condemns the header it does not raise. The reading date is one of four bound facts, and the footer's own Bound stamp names them: workspace, owner, reading date and the 9. Driven in loading, .ws prints 'Harbour House weddings - Orla' at rgb(113,113,122) - the same ink, the same header, the same state as the stamp the seat calls a lie. Workspace and owner are no more 'held' by a state that is still reading than the reading date is. Both are bound, neither is read, and only one is filed. That is the test that killed bound-nine-prints-where-no-nine-was-read in r2. (3) Two supporting claims are false when driven. 'At full ink': the reading line computes to rgb(113,113,122), Geist Mono 11px 400, ink-3 - identical in all seven states, and the dim label voice. 'Above a page that has been emptied of every other fact': in loading, movementThree renders whole at full ink - .limit .t-head computes to rgb(17,17,17) - so the refusals, not the stamp, are the strongest text on that page. (4) Round 2's rule is honoured, not skipped. The rule at lately.html:1222-1226 is scoped to .sk-wrap because that is what the skeleton is - the same DOM with its ink out. The footer and the reading line are chrome, outside main and outside the skeleton, and the skeleton's own magnitudes ARE neutralised: bars to --h:46, meters to --f:0.4, dots evenly spaced, .record/.record-tag/.fortnight hidden, .sr lines removed, controls made inert, the whole block aria-hidden. Nothing regressed. WHY THE FIX IS WORSE. 'Make the Read entry a source like the other three' fails on its own terms: Read is not a source, it is an instant, and the row renders as READ READING - measured, all four widths. It is not a phrase in any of the three grammars on that strip. Meanwhile BOUND ... READING DATE AND THE 9 would keep claiming a bound reading date on a page that no longer prints one. And the fix's load-bearing promise - 'Both keep their box, their rank and their place, so no geometry moves when the data lands' - is measurably false at the width the brief calls the whole reading on a phone. Applying both strings in place at 390x900 and re-running the surface's own wrap measurement: .reading un-wraps (data-wrapped true to false, height 61.69px to 38.84px, the connector rule reappears and the interpunct separators vanish), .coverage drops from 5 rows to 4 (122.06px to 103.22px) and document height falls 2664 to 2622px - a 42px jump the moment the data lands, in a state built so the surface cannot jump when the data lands. At 768/1280/1440 nothing moves; at 390 everything below the header does. Severity is overstated on top of that: nothing untrue is asserted and nothing is visibly wrong, so refinement at most, and I do not think the refinement is worth taking.

refuted.problem: A job's title exists in exactly one place on this screen: the tip raised by hover, focus or a tap. Nothing at rest says the marks are pressable. Screenshotting `.card.ages` on its own at 1440 ?state=full, the whole card is: the heading "How long open work has been sitting", an "OLDEST · 41 DAYS" stamp, a dashed fortnight rule with its label, nine 12px discs, a hairline axis and four ticks. No legend, no instruction, no rest-state name — the only affordance is `cursor: pointer`, which does not exist under a coarse pointer, and a 2px ring/fill difference that reads as a data encoding (inside vs past the fortnight), not as a control. The accessibility tree is better served than the screen: every `aria-label` carries "<title>, open N days", so a screen-reader user is handed all nine titles and a sighted phone reader is handed none. Driven at 390 with touch, a tap does raise and pin the tip correctly — the mechanism is there and works; the invitation is missing.
refuted.why: The observation is accurate and the fix and the class are both wrong, which is what decides it. Driven in chromium at 1440x960 and at 390x844 with touch, ?v=light, states full/quiet/first-run/loading, I enumerated every visible text node inside .card.ages: at 1440 it is exactly "How long open work has been sitting", "OLDEST · 41 DAYS", "A FORTNIGHT", and the ticks today/15d/30d/45d, over six hollow and three solid discs; at 390 the same seven strings in a 342x263 card. So the seat is right that no rest-state string names a job and none names the interaction, and right that the .sr paragraph and the nine aria-labels leave the AX tree richer than the screen. Three things then break it. (1) THE FIX IS IN THE WRONG VOICE AND WOULD MAKE THE CARD WORSE. .t-label is lately.html:150 — 11px Geist Mono, letter-spacing var(--track-label), text-transform: uppercase. The proposed paragraph renders as EACH MARK IS ONE JOB — PRESS ONE FOR ITS NAME: forty-four characters of tracked uppercase mono with an em dash inside it. On this surface the label voice is a two-to-four-word stamp (OLDEST · 41 DAYS, A FORTNIGHT, THREE REFUSALS, NOT YET); no sentence is set in it anywhere. Worse, .dim resolves to --ink-3, the identical ink .strip-scale already paints its ticks in (lately.html:415), and the line would land immediately beneath that row of mono ticks — a second mono voice, shouting, in the same colour, one line under the first. It would read as another axis annotation, not as an invitation, which is the one job it was added to do. The inline margin-top:var(--gap-snug) is also a one-off outside the card's own rhythm (.ages sets its gaps at --gap-room/--gap-line). Both automated gates would stay green on this fix — data-type="label" is a legal role and #71717a on paper clears AA — which is exactly why it has to be caught by eye. (2) THE CLASS IS OVERSTATED. Nothing on this card is wrong or untrue. Every mark is placed by value, ringed to clear the 3:1 non-text floor, named in the tree, and raises its tip on pointer, keyboard and touch — interaction-check.mjs proves all three paths ("a real pointer over a mark names it", "a real touch on a mark names it", the second-tap dismiss, Escape). The seat says so itself: "the mechanism is there and works". An under-advertised affordance that works is a refinement, not a defect — and detail-on-demand with no instruction line is precisely what the named benchmarks ship: Stripe's dashboard, Vercel Analytics and Linear's insights all raise a tooltip off a mark, on touch as well as pointer, with no "press me" copy on the canvas. Grading this a defect grades the surface against a convention the benchmarks do not themselves follow. (3) THE CONSEQUENCE IS INFLATED. "WHICH three" is not "the one fact the movement was built to deliver". Movement two's stated deliverable is the counts, all five out of the same nine, plus the shape of the ages; the identity of an individual job is the Tasks destination that the round notes put on the port packet and that round 2 deliberately stopped promising. The tip is a bonus detail layer over a movement that already answers its question in the KPI row above it.

refuted.problem: `.bar-val` carries no animation. It is positioned from `--h` at first paint, so at `?motion=play` it is at opacity 1, in its final place, from frame one — while the column it labels is still flat on the baseline. Driven at 1440, state=full: at t=100ms the label's top is 290px and its bar's top is 479px (the baseline) at 0px height; at 340ms and 620ms the bar is still 0px and the label is still at 283px; the bar first shows height at 780ms (28.4px) and only reaches full at ~1280ms. So for the first ~780ms of a 1.7s entrance the one indigo mark in movement one hangs at the top of an empty plot with nothing beneath it. In state=first-run the plot holds that single column and nothing else, so for the first ~340ms the chart is a floating indigo "12 so far" over blank white — the first frame a new customer sees. The rest of the choreography is disciplined about exactly this: `.record-tag` is held to 1.5s so the previous-best tag arrives after its own rule draws at 1.1s. The live week's value was left out of that ordering.
refuted.why: The mechanism is real and the timings are accurate, but the three perceptual claims the consequence rests on are all measurably false, and stripping them leaves a refinement, not a defect. Driven in chromium at 1440, ?motion=play, sampling deterministically by pausing every animation and pinning currentTime (page.clock drifts the document timeline; the seat's numbers survive that correction). CONFIRMED: document.getAnimations() returns 0 animations whose target is .bar-val, in full and in first-run. The live bar (i=11) is animation-delay 0.78s / 0.5s, so lastBar height is 0.0px at T=780 and 168px at T=1280; in first-run the solo bar (i=0) is 0.34s/0.5s. Every number the seat quotes checks out. REFUTED on three counts. (1) 'at opacity 1, in its final place, from frame one' is false. The label lives inside .card.hero.rise, which is rise 0.5s backwards at 65ms. Measured card opacity: 0 at T=0, 0.288 at T=100, 0.805 at T=200, 0.978 at T=340 — and the label's own top is 293.0px at T=0, 290.1 at 100, 285.0 at 200, 283.0 at 500. So at frame one it is at opacity 0 and 10px below its final place; it arrives on the card's rise with the hero number, the delta pill, the sentence and the note, exactly like everything else in the card. It is not early to the frame — it is early to its column only. (2) 'hangs at the top of an empty plot with nothing beneath it' is false for state=full. Counting bars with painted height >1px: 0 at T=340, 4 at T=500, 7 at T=620, 11 at T=780. The plot is not empty for 780ms; it is mid-sweep, and the label sits over the last slot of a left-to-right sweep that has visibly reached it. In the 620ms frame the reader is watching columns arrive and the indigo label reads as the destination of the sweep, not as an orphan. (3) 'a floating indigo 12 so far over blank white' in first-run is false. At T=100/200/340 the card is at 0.288/0.805/0.978 opacity and carries the hero '12', 'jobs finished since you started, Harbour House weddings', the comparison-arrives note, the 57px baseline and the '13 JUL' tick, all rising together; the label is one element on a card that is itself arriving, and the actual first frame a new customer sees is opacity 0. What is left after the corrections is that the live week's value paints with the chart's LABEL RAIL rather than with its mark — and the rail is what the source says it belongs to (.chart comment, lately.html:243: 'A label rail on the right. The axis maximum, the previous-best tag and the live week's value all anchor to this edge'). The gridline value labels '12' and '6' are static and also present before any column exists, in the same band, 34px to the right. A rail label arriving with its scale is a defensible reading, not something visibly wrong. The .record-tag precedent does not carry the weight the seat puts on it either: a dashed rule that has not drawn leaves its tag pointing at nothing, whereas a right-rail value 6px above where its column will end is pointing at its own slot. SEVERITY overstated: this is 'refinement' (nothing is wrong), not 'defect' (visibly wrong but passable), and the brief makes an overstated class a reason to refute. THE FIX also fails on its own description and on first-run. Patched into a staged copy and measured: with --i emitted the live label computes animation-delay 1.24s in full and 0.8s in first-run, which is the arithmetic the seat claims. But 'it lands as the mark completes' is wrong — with a 0.35s rise starting at 1240ms the label reaches opacity 1 at 1590ms, measured 0.447 at T=1280 and 0.952 at T=1400, i.e. 310ms AFTER the column completes, not at it. And in first-run the fix is a net loss: the solo column is fully drawn at 840ms while the label is at 0.447 opacity and does not land until 1150ms, so the one screen the finding calls the new customer's first frame gains a ~300ms fully-opaque frame of a full-height indigo hatched column carrying no value at all, and the label becomes the last thing that moves on a card whose entire subject it is. Trading a label-without-mark for a mark-without-label on that exact screen, and stretching first-run's entrance from 840ms to 1150ms to do it, is not an improvement at this bar. To the seat's credit, two of its safety claims check out: no overprint was produced against .gridline b or .record-tag at any sampled entrance frame, and [data-motion="settled"], prefers-reduced-motion and [data-state="loading"] do zero the new animation, so no graded frame changes.

refuted.problem: "Sitting" is used exactly twice on the whole surface, both times as a `.t-head` at the same typographic rank, both inside the same section, and it means opposite things. Measured at 1440, ?state=quiet: "Nothing is sitting" at y=739, "How long open work has been sitting" at y=963 — 224px apart, no other heading between them. In the first it means "stalled past a fortnight"; in the second it means "open". Under the second heading the card then draws nine marks and prints "Oldest · 12 days". Every other place the surface names this idea it says it precisely — the KPI card says "haven't moved in a fortnight", the spoken line says "open longer than a fortnight" — so the loose word appears only where it collides with itself.
refuted.why: Every measurement in the finding is right and the conclusion built on them is not. Driven in chromium at file://.../lately.html?v=light&state=quiet at 1440x960 with reduced motion: 'Nothing is sitting' is a P.t-head at document y=739, 20px/600, ink #111111, inside section[aria-labelledby=m2q]; 'How long open work has been sitting' is an H3.t-head at y=963, 20px/600, ink #111111, same section; 963-739=224px, and the heading list between them is empty (t-sect at 576, then nothing until 'What this can't tell you' at 1213). 'sitting' matches exactly twice in main.innerText in quiet and exactly once in full, partial, first-run and loading. The ages card reads 'Oldest - 12 days' over nine dots at ages 1,2,3,4,6,7,9,11,12, zero of them .old. So the seat's geometry, ranks and counts are all correct. What fails is the premise. The finding has to assign 'sitting' a technical meaning in the first heading - 'stalled past a fortnight' - to make the second heading collide with it, and the surface never says that. It says the fortnight idea precisely everywhere it means it: the KPI card is 'haven't moved in a fortnight', the spoken line is 'open longer than a fortnight', and the quiet body directly under the headline is 'All 9 open jobs have moved inside a fortnight, none is past its day, every one has a name on it, and none is waiting on anything else.' The finding cites that same precision as evidence for itself ('every other place the surface names this idea it says it precisely') without noticing it is evidence against: 'sitting' is precisely NOT the technical term on this surface, it is the informal umbrella for work left unattended - which is the identical sense the ages heading uses. One sense, two scopes, not two senses and certainly not 'opposite'; the finding's own body concedes the second is a superset of the first ('stalled past a fortnight' vs 'open'), which is not what its title claims. Second, the pair is claim-and-proof, not claim-and-refutation. I looked at the rendered band rather than arguing about it: below 'Nothing is sitting' the ages card draws all nine rings to the LEFT of a drawn, labelled 'A FORTNIGHT' rule at 14d on a 15d axis, oldest at 12, and speaks '0 jobs have been open longer than a fortnight.' The card the finding calls the contradiction is the receipt. That is exactly what the r1 remediation of quiet-state-contradicts-its-own-evidence was built to produce (that state used to show 41 days and three .old marks under the same headline), and this finding does not claim a regression and there is none. Third, severity is overstated, which the brief makes a refutation ground on its own. Nothing on the screen is wrong: both headings are true, the marks prove the claim, the threshold is drawn. 'Defect' means visibly wrong but passable; this is at most a word echo a copy editor might tighten, which is 'refinement - nothing is wrong'. The lab's own ledger settles the calibration: the-all-clear-sentence-drops-one-of-its-four-categories (r2) was a strictly more substantive gap in THIS card - a whole condition genuinely unsaid - and was confirmed at refinement on the reasoning 'the sentence asserts nothing untrue, so it is not misleading, and it is not a defect'. Grading a two-use echo a defect would rank it above an actually-missing clause. Worth adding against the consequence as written ('read cold... the surface contradicting itself'): at the shipped frame size the second heading's top is at y=963 against a 960px viewport, so the two are not even co-visible in light-quiet--1440x960.png without a scroll. Fourth, the fix is a downgrade. 'Nothing is slipping' 163px under the 26px section heading 'What's quietly slipping' echoes the container's own word back at it, and trades the warmer, physical, owner-voiced line - the one paired with the emerald check in the single state whose job is to be believed - for the surface's abstract category label. The lexical bridge from the all-clear to the strip is already 'fortnight' (the body says 'moved inside a fortnight'; the strip draws the rule), not 'sitting', so nothing is gained on that side either. The one genuinely valuable thing in this filing is the gate observation, and it is worth more than the copy edit and is independent of it - see sharpenedFix.

refuted.problem: The note reads: "Timeline did not answer this reading, so nothing here knows a due date. The card keeps its place and says so; it does not fall back to zero." The first sentence is the owner's. The second is the studio's — it names a component ("the card"), describes a layout decision ("keeps its place") and defends a policy to a reviewer ("it does not fall back to zero"). r1 closed refusals-written-in-the-studio-vocabulary on the three limit tiles; the class is back, in a different element, and the paid defect library records it as raised three separate times in one previous engagement.
refuted.why: Driven in chromium at ?state=partial, 1440/1280/768/390, light and dark. The quote is exact (lately.html:870) and every load-bearing claim built on it is wrong. (1) The consequence's headline claim - 'it is the only place on this surface where the product talks about itself' - is false in the very state it was raised against. The same frame carries 'Counted at the moment each job reached a done column.' (hero note, lately.html:823), the whole third movement in that register ('Nothing was written down about how much was open in earlier weeks', 'nothing keeps a record of it yet', 'That would be a change in Notes'), the ghost caption ('Once open work starts being counted each week, it fills in after about a month.'), and a coverage footer that prints TASKS ANSWERED / TIMELINE DID NOT ANSWER / LAB COUNTS AND AGES ARE LAB-AUTHORED / BOUND WORKSPACE, OWNER, READING DATE AND THE 9. A product that reports on its own reading is this surface's register, and the movement that carries it is a protected object. The note is inside that register, not an outlier in it. (2) 'It tells them nothing they can act on' fails on measurement. In the partial KPI row the '-' card sits at x=646 and a genuine '0 | are waiting on something else' card sits at x=1086 - a real zero and a real unavailable, same row, same type ramp, 440px apart. 'It does not fall back to zero' is the only sentence on the visible surface that separates them, and separating them is the literal wording of the protected honest-degradation contract ('A reader can never mistake "we don't know" for "it's zero"'). The card's own furniture says '-' and 'NOT AVAILABLE'; neither says 'not zero'. (3) The class citation is misapplied. refusals-written-in-the-studio-vocabulary (r1) was engineering nouns and verbs - 'snapshot writer', 'callers', 'date recorder', 'accrues', 'three periods' - plus a 'we' that appeared nowhere else; lessons.md scopes the paid class as 'The studio's private vocabulary in the accessibility tree. Internal names are not product names.' No internal name appears here, and nothing in the accessibility tree is touched: the card's name is 'Jobs past the day they were due: not available, because Timeline did not answer', which is plain. 'Card' is the ordinary English word for the object the reader is looking at, not a component name leaked from source. The class has not regressed; a different sentence in the same register was found and called by the old name. (4) The fix would make the work worse and commits the defect it names. 'Everything else on this page was read normally' is itself the product narrating its own reading, so it does not cure the stated problem; 'read normally' is further from the owner's language than 'does not fall back to zero' ('normally' against what norm?); it duplicates the coverage footer, which already prints TASKS ANSWERED and NOTES ANSWERED, FOR YOU four hundred pixels below; and it deletes the only foreclosure of the zero-misreading in a row that visibly contains a zero. It is billed as 'the owner's next fact' and is not a fact about her venue at all. (5) Severity. The seat classed this refinement, which the brief defines as 'nothing is wrong', and this round's instruction is explicit that a refinement is not to be raised to have raised something. The cost is one wrapped line at 1280/1440 (note is 3 lines, 79px) and two at 390 (5 lines, 125px) - measured, not asserted.
